entries.title: The Missing Years: 2015-2019
entries.author: Chairman Rand Paul
entries.provenance: Publisher's cover and analysis printed on page 1 of the release (a scan, transcribed with macOS Vision OCR). Not one of the released documents.
entries.content:
The Missing Years: 2015-2019

EARLY-ONSET TRUMP DERANGEMENT SYNDROME.
Before Trump took office, Dr. Fauci wrote he was "more and more concerned about even talking to the transition people

about being NIH Director since Trump is so unpredictable" (January 1-5, 2017). The day after the inauguration, he noted that

his wife marched against Trump in Washington and his daughters in Boston and San Francisco, and called the new President
"amaxingly [sic] unpresidential!" (January 21, 2017). By March, the White House staff were "a scary bunch" and "Trump and
his people are truly unscrupulous. This is outrageous!" (March 10-16, 2017). By 2019 he had a verdict: Trump "is acting more
and more bizarre. Should be impeached, but Dems are rightfully concerned that this will galvanize his base

(January 1-7, 2019).

PUBLIC PRAISE. PRIVATE DOUBTS.
When the World Health Organization declared its 2015 Ebola vaccine trial a 100% effective "breakthrough," Dr. Fauci privately
wrote of "multiple flaws in the design and the analysis of the data" and a "terribly flawed study design." He went on CNN,
BBC, and PBS anyway and told the New York Times the results were "very encouraging" and "impressive," noting in his diary
that he had given a "congratulatory comment" while "slipping in the fact that the data, strictly speaking, are not statistically
significant." His reasoning: "I am leaning heavily towards praise for the study. We cannot criticize the study since that is
exactly what the press is looking for and then they will create a tension between HHS and WHO. HHS is too stupid to realize

that" (July 31, 2015).

RANSOMWARE ATTACK WIPED HIS CONFIDENTIAL FILES.

An entry from the summer of 2016 notes: "MISSING MATERIAL (Ransomware hack) ... will try to backfill." Dr. Fauci later

explained that his "entire unprotected folder" was encrypted and he "lost all of the letters that I have ever written as well as
other important documents." The folder was created for "the confidential files that I made right after the anthrax attacks
since I did not want them accessible to anyone." His verdict: "Bad idea!!!" (July 22, 2016).

"I CANNOT SEE WHY THIS IS SO SECRET."
After being shown Senate Intelligence Committee documents on agents that induce cytokine storms "for which we have no
countermeasures," Dr. Fauci noted that chasing every bioterror threat meant "fighting windmills" (November 22, 2017). After
a "highest top secret level" classified discussion that China was "stealing our technologies for Ebola vaccines and therapies,"
he wrote: "I cannot see why this is so secret. This stuff is in the literature and in clinicaltrials.gov" (January 16, 2019).
Presented with "believable intell" on foreign bioterror programs, he wrote: "I have heard this story multiple times over
the years .... and they have never panned out" (March 26, 2019). Weeks before news of the COVID-19 outbreak went public,
the National Security Council summoned him to the SCIF because of his "knowledge and standing and because I am Tony

Fauci" (December 6, 2019).

"BIG CHINESE VISITOR DAY."

Dr. Fauci hosted China CDC Director General George Gao at NIH ("Very smart and nice guy. Almost recruited to the VRC many

years ago"), then met China's Vice Premier, Health Minister, and the head of the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences at
CSIS: "I gave brief description of activities of NIH in collaboration with Chinese" (September 27, 2017).

NOT JUST THE SCHEDULER

Patricia Conrad, Dr. Fauci's long-time special assistant, was not just keeping his calendar; she also attended high-level

meetings with him. She joined Dr. Fauci in the Dirksen office of Senator Richard Burr, then Chairman of the Senate
Intelligence Committee, alongside ASPR Nicki Lurie, BARDA chief Richard Hatchett, Bob Kadlec, and Burr's chief staffer, as
the Senator vented that he created BARDA and "now every time there is a global health emergency, we ask for emergency
funds," and that the administration was "trying to steal from the BioShield account" (April 28, 2016).

Getting into the summer and ready for the IAS meeting in Vancouver.   I
have prepared very well for a talk of Comprehensive HIV prevention.
Gave my almost-every-year talk to the St.Alban’s Summer School of Public Service.   I 
talk on “my career as a public servant.   Always fun.   Enthusiastic students – high school 
from all over USA.
Met with people from Gene Tech wanted to get NIAID interested in a product.   Lobbyist 
was Tommy Thompson.   Could not say no to them since it is Tommy whom I love.   
Great memories of when he was HHS Secretary.

Had teleconference in Building 1, Room 116 with activists who were
concerned about the OAR budget (see above with Senator Cassidy).   Also, they are not 
sure that Francis Collins will really fight to sustain the AIDS/OAR budget.   Also, they 
are concerned now that Jack Whitescarver has retired, who will be the OAR Director.   I 
have been convincing Francis that he really cannot decrease the AIDS budget to move 
money to other areas, even though deep down that is exactly what he wants to do.   He is 
playing some politics in trying to ingratiate himself with the conservatives; however, in 
fairness to him, he does have a point about the disparity favoring AIDS research over 
others.   On the call were Francis, Larry Tabak, Kathy Hudson, Jim Anderson, Bob 
Eisinger and activists → Mark Harrington, Peter Staley, Gregg Gonsalves, Mitch Warren, 
Lynda Dee, Jim Eigo, Kevin Frost (amFAR), Phill Wilson, among others.   Friendly call.   
They really wanted a commitment to keep AIDS funding at 10% of NIH; however, 
Francis (with my encouragement) could not really promise that due to the ear-marks with 
NIH increases to other areas.   However, I got Francis to agree that the scientific 
opportunities would dictate any increases in AIDS budget.   Also, it would not get any 
smaller.

Met with Nicki Lurie, Lu Borio, Robin Robinson and Cliff Lane in 7A-
24 to discuss the ongoing situation in Guinea and West Africa regarding the ZMapp 
therapy trial and the Ebola vaccine studies.   Cliff now up to >50 patients on the RCT for 
ZMapp.   MSF still refusing to participate (they are against randomized trials even though 
the expanded/free access of Favipiravir and Brincidofavir have resulted in from nothing 
to disaster (toxicity).
Also me with Slim and Quarraisha Karim in 7A-24.   He wants NIAID support for a  
CAP256 (bNAb) trial in RSA.   John Mascola was present at meeting since he helped 
make the antibody.

Griff Rogers and Josie Briggs will chair the Search Committee for the
OAR.   I met with them today to get them to understand that there is misperception out 
there that the OAR head will be the Chief HIV person at the NIH and as we know that 
just is not the case and so there should not be any unrealistic expectations when someone 
is applying for the job as to what their responsibility will be.
Had dinner at my house with Charles Dinarello who was in town with one of his Dutch 
colleagues for a lecture.  Charles has not changed a bit.   He is wonderfully crazy, 
paranoid about not getting credit for his discoveries (he is correct since I believe that he 
should have won the Nobel Prize for discovering and cloning IL-1B.

Gave major lecture (on July 20) at the IAS meeting in Vancouver.
Lectured on “Progress and Challenges in HIV prevention:  Non-Vaccine and Vaccine 
Approaches”.   Lecture went over extremely well.   I could not help but reflect and 
comment in my lecture that 19 years ago, almost to the day, the first triple combination 
ART regimens with indinavir (protease inhibitor) + AZT + 3TC was presented at the 
1996 Vancouver IAS meeting by Roy (Trip) Gulick and others.   That was a transforming 
meeting since it began the era of HAART that turned around the field of HIV/AIDS.   
Now here in Vancouver, we see 15 million people on ARVs (largely through PEPFAR, 
Global Fund and others) and we are showing that you should start everyone at any CD4 
count (START Study) and that Treatment as prevention (TasP – HPTN-052) really works 
as does PrEP.    Another transforming meeting – 19 years later. 
On Tuesday (21 July) flew to San Francisco to have dinner with Ali.   Saw her office at 
Twitter.  She is doing great.  Training for a marathon.

Had lunch at French Embassy with Professor Genevieve Chene of
Viesan and Claire Aubin Counsellor at the Embassy and Mireille Guyader, Director of 
the USA INSERM Bureaus to discuss potential collaborations between INSERM and 
NIH.  Beautiful few days in DC.   Sunny, clear and no humidity!

Went to New Orleans today to visit Megan recently moved there after
leaving Philadelphia. It was great to see her; however, it was oppressively hot. She is 
living in a really nice little studio apartment in a neighborhood just outside of French 
quarter. Stayed there until Sunday and flew back with Chris who had gone down one day 
earlier than I.

Went to dinner tonight at the Jefferson Hotel in the Wine Room as a
guest of Catherine and Wayne Reynolds. It was the typical Catherine and Wayne social 
event with many interesting guess. I had the opportunity to sit next to Brent Scowcroft 
and we spoke about our common friend President George H.W. Bush.  Brent is a 
wonderful elderly gentleman who has experience extraordinary times during his many 
years of government service. We spoke about the situation in Iran as well as in China. It 
so happened that the Chinese stock market lost about 10% of its value today, which is 
equivalent to a crash. Also at the dinner was Ben Carson who was running for president 
and who was taken to task by several people, mostly Democrats, at the dinner for his 
recent public statement that the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare) was the worst thing to 
happen to the country since slavery. Ben then described his version of healthcare. He was 
getting blasted, and then I interjected and told him in front of the entire dinner table that 
although we have been old friends for a long time and that I respected his views even 
though I disagreed with many of them, his statement was in fact spectacularly unfair to 
the Obama administration. Several people at the table later told me that that was the most 
important thing that was said that night. Also at the dinner were Valerie Jarrett, Rick 
Atkinson, Eric Holder, John Negroponte, and an up and coming young African-American 
female lawyer named Angela Dry.  Angela was particularly impressed with my statement 
to Ben Carson.  Again, another terrific evening with Catherine and Wayne Reynolds.

Agnes Binagwaho, Health Minister of Rwanda, visited NIH and I went
to her lecture in Masur Auditorium, met with her and her staff in my office and had 
dinner with her at La Ferme in Chevy Chase.   We struck up a quick and warm 
relationship.   I am pushing her (and she is responding as she feels the same way as I do) 
to truly try to end the AIDS epidemic in Rwanda.   We will work together to develop a 
formula as to how to do that.   She was accompanied by two young women (extremely 
accomplished already) who will start Harvard Medical School on August 2 and look upon 
me as a “legend”.   They were delighted to meet me.  Names: Kirstin Scott and Claire 
Wagner.   They have been working for 1 to 3 years with Agnes as her personal staff.   
They are on their way to stardom.

Announcement of the “success” of the Ring vaccination trial for Ebola in
Guinea made today by WHO.   17 infections in the delayed ring and 0 infections in the 
immediate ring.   WHO selling this as a 100% effective breakthrough.   Problem is that 
there are multiple flaws in the design and the analysis of the data that Phil Krause of FDA 
beautifully articulated.   Bottom line is that we are dealing with an inherently good and 
effective vaccine that was put into a terribly flawed study design.   And so now they 
(WHO, Norwegians, MSF) are claiming victory for the study, when it is the vaccine that 
could have proven effective in any study since it is so good.   Such is life….
I gave congratulatory comment in the NY Times (Sheri Fink – reporter today) while still 
slipping in the fact that the data, strictly speaking, are not statistically significant.
I appeared on CNN with Wolf Blitzer, BBC and PBS NewsHour.   HHS COMMs (Leah 
Hunter) is getting all bent out of shape trying to micromanage what I say on TV and even 
tried to shut me down on TV but I appealed to Leslie Dach who gave me the go-ahead.   
HHS cannot decide whether they want to praise the study, give strong caveats or both.   I 
believe that I am giving the right balance. I am leaning heavily towards praise for the 
study.   We cannot criticize the study since that is exactly what the press is looking for 
and then they will create a tension between HHS and WHO.   HHS is too stupid to realize 
that.

Appeared on CNN New Day this AM at 7:40 to discuss the outbreak of
Legionnaire’s Disease in NYC (South Bronx) with 81 cases and 7 deaths.   Outbreak 
related to contaminated cooling towers on the top of buildings.   Reminiscent of the 1976 
outbreak at the Bellevue-Stratford Hotel in Philadelphia.   Again getting shit from HHS 
COMMS people (Leah Hunter) demanding “talking points” before she approves my 
going on TV, Radio, or Print.   I am just going to go ahead without asking clearance.
Also, just did CNN with Wolf Blitzer.   Wolf was not there.   Had a sub → Brianna 
Keilar.

Things in NYC still hot with the Legionella outbreak.   Now there are
100 cases and 10 deaths.  Gov. Cuomo calling in the CDC to the anger of DiBlasio and 
Mary Bassett (NYC Health Commissioner) since they feel that NYC can handle this 
themselves.   Did CBS Radio News.

Media still hot for the NYC Legionella story.  Staring to see friction
between Governor Cuomo and Mayor DiBlasio in that Cuomo is calling for the CDC to 
come in (suggesting that the NYC health authorities are not responding well enough).  
Also, Cuomo is offering free inspection of all cooling towers on roofs.  I appeared on 
MSNBC TV and CBS Radio (NYC).

Legionella still in the news.   113 cases and 12 deaths.   I appeared on
WTOP Radio with Mike Moss and Joan Jones at 6:40 AM yesterday (08/10/15).

DiBlasio and Cuomo have been criticized in the press for aquabbling
with each other and are saying that the people wind up suffering when the authorities are 
fighting with each other.
I appear on CBS News (NYC) about Legionella, but I do not get into the 
DiBlasio/Cuomo arguments.

Met today in my office with Dr. Mohamed Lamine Yansane the
Counsellor for Piblic health in the Ministry of Health in Guinea and Professor Many 
Kader Konde, well known Guinean physician and president of Foundation Santi & 
Developpement Durable (FOSAD) in Guinea.   Translation by Ydrissa Sow.  Cliff Lane 
was present.   They are in USA for meetings and were delighted to drop by.   They 
praised Cliff for his work in Guinea and confirmed that Cliff was the only foreign health 
person who actually involved the host people in discussions before doing something in 
Guinea.   They were “greatly honored” to meet me and want very much for me to visit 
Guinea.

Mark Harrington had sent me an e-mail asking to have dinner at a
restaurant in DC since he and several activists wanted to discuss several AIDS issues 
including the search for the new OAR director to replace Jack Whitescarver as well as 
my recent talks on ending the AIDS epidemic and how they could help, at least in NYC 
or even globally.   I suggested that we meet at my house and I cooked my famous 
Sausage and rigatoni with Caesar salad, Italian bread, appetizers (olives, dips, brie 
cheese) and Sicilian Pistachio and Coffee Chocolate Chip ice cream.   Santa Margherita 
Pinot Grigio and Coppola Pinot Noir.   The weather over the past several days has been 
gorgeous with Fall-like evenings.   Unfortunately, tonight was muggy and it rained.  And 
so we sat in the TV room for appetizers and went to the main dining room for dinner.   
Present were Mark Harrington, Peter Staley, David Barr, Mitch Warren, Moises Agosto, 
and Kenyon Farrow (Global Health head at TAG) and Carl Dieffenbach.   Gregg 
Gonsalves was supposed to come, but he is at Yale and with the new school year starting, 
he could not come.   Lively, friendly discussions.   We reminisced some about prior 
dinners during the “years” of the activist movement at Jim Hill’s house.   Interesting, that 
my good friend Peter Staley expressed concern that since I was 74 years old, what was 
going to happen to the field and the efforts when I retire.   I told him not to worry since I 
will not retire for several years and/or until the epidemic is clearly on the way down.
Of note, over the past few days the Stock Market has been crashing (down almost 2500 
points in 1 week!!!) due to the crashing of the Chinese economy and the devaluating of 
their currency.

Stock Market stabilizing, but still now where near rebounding to the
pre-crash level”.  Had meeting in Medical Board Room  (Room 4-2551) of Building 10 
with the new OMB Associate Director for Health Programs Adaeze Akamigbo and her 
assistant Sarah Haile for a “meet and greet” to brief her on the NIH.   At the briefing were 
Francis Collins, Larry Tabak, Kathy Hudson, Mitchell Goldstein of HHS, Doug Lowy 
and me.   Key issue is that Francis used the opportunity to emphasize that he is against a 
10% set aside for AIDS and that after re-reprioritization, he felt the AIDS allocation 
should probably decrease.   He did not explicitly say that, but clearly he was hinting it.   
If the activists were in the room, they would have gone ballistic.

Had wonderful trip to San Francisco, then up the coast to Mendocino,
then down through the Napa Valley to celebrate our 30th Wedding Anniversary.   Ali 
joined us.   When in SF, stayed at Bob Grady’s home at 15 Sea Cliff Avenue.  First night 
in SF had cocktails at amazing rooftop bar called “Techo” with great view of the city.
In Mendocino, stayed at a magical resort called Heritage House Resort with spectacular 
view of the Pacific Ocean and its cliff-like shores.   In Napa stopped at Coppola Vineyard 
and Robert Mondavi Vineyard for wine tasting.  Met Rick Ayre and Barbara Grady at the 
Mondavi Vineyard.   Last night in SF went to the Mission district and had dinner at one 
of Ali’s favorite restaurants (broken down place, but charming.

Gave closing remarks at a ceremony at the White House (South Court
Auditorium) to celebrate 25th Anniversary of the Ryan White CARE Act.   Horribly hot 
(but sunny) day in DC.   Waited on line for almost 1 hour to get into WH.   Finally, 
people from NAPO had to “rescue” me and get me in more quickly.   Speakers at 
ceremony were:   Doug Brooks, Surgeon General Vivek Murthy, Jean Flatley, Tim 
Westmoreland, Henry Waxman, Senator Orin Hatch, Senator Joe Donnelly, Jeanne White 
–Ginder (Ryan’s mother) and 2 panels.   Many AIDS friends were there including Eric
Goosby, Jack Whitescarver.   I spoke about the relationship of our attempts to end the
AIDS pandemic and the important of the Ryan White CARE Act and program.

Gave Plenary Lecture at the Annual Meeting of the U.S. Conference on
AIDS held at the Marriott Marquis on 9th Street and Mass Avenue, NW.   Spoke on 
ending the AIDS pandemic.   Large crowd of >1000.   Very receptive to me – large 
proportion of gay men.   Not the usual scientific crowd that I speak to – mostly 
community based people.   Also on program was Nancy Pelosi, Doug Brooks and Kate 
Burton, Richard Burton’s daughter and Elizabeth Taylor’s step-daughter.   
here in DC when he visited a few years ago, but he was unquestionably my best friend at 
Regis.   Brave guy.   Taking it very philosophically.

Gepi Pantaleo in town for a day from Lausanne.  Went to dinner at a
different restaurant than the usual Café Milano.  Went to Fiola Mare in Georgetown 
waterfront.   Great meal.   Good to see Gepi.

Went to Duke to give Keynote Lecture at Bart Haynes’s CHAVI-ID 10th
Anniversary meeting.   Spoke on “Ending the AIDS Epidemic with Non-Vaccine and 
Vaccine Prevention methods”.   Quick trip.

Cliff Lane and I went to a small IOM meeting at the Keck Center (500
5th Street, NW) as a follow-up of the Hong Kong meeting that we (the USG) people 
missed because they called it without even consulting with us and then they realized that 
they did not have any senior USG people at the meeting.   Tachi Yamada and Maria 
Freire chaired the meeting.   Also present were: Nicki Lurie (ASPR), Ed Cox, Lu Borio, 
Phil Krause and Rob Califf (FDA), Beth Bell (CDC), Susan Sherman (HHS).   Purpose 
was to try to reconcile some of the disagreements between us and the WHO (Marie-Paule 
Kieny), Wellcome Trust (Jeremy Farrar) that had surfaced regarding the conduct of 
clinical trials in West Africa with the Ebola epidemic.   Meeting went well.   We just 
firmly maintained that the USG (mostly NIH and FDA) would only be involved in 
clinical trials that are scientifically sound and that would come up with a scientifically 
defensible conclusion.

Attended
Uplifting talking about his character
Spt. 29, 2015 – Went to Baltimore to receive the “Lifetime Achievement Award” from 
Bob Gallo’s Institute for Human Virology.   Other recipient was Nobel Prize winner 
Harald zur Hausen.   Bart Haynes and Cliff Lane gave a very nice introduction of me 
talking about my character, accomplishments, etc.   Good evening.   Unfortunately, I 
developed   except when I was receiving 
the award and giving my Keynote earlier in the afternoon (Adrenaline).

Participated in a panel for the Washington Ideas Festival (Sponsored by
Atlantic magazine.   Incredible cast of people – the entire “in crowd” in DC.   I was on 
the panel with Vanessa Kerry (daughter of Joh Kerry) and the panel was moderated by 
NPR anchor Mary Louise Kelly.   Topic was Global Health.   Kerry was very gracious to 
me saying that it was a highest honor for her to appear with me.
Following the Panel, I went to the Kennedy Caucus Room of the Russell Senate Building 
to observe the launching of the Kennedy Oral History Program.   There was a speech by 
historian/author Michael Beschloss and a great panel chaired by Judy Woodruff and 
including Alan Simpson, Chis Dodd, Melody Barnes, Margaret Spellings and Barbara 
Perry.  Got a chance to chat with Vicki Kennedy and Chris Dodd.   Very moving 
remembrances of Teddy.   Time well-spent.

Discovery Channel interview for big story on the NIH Clinical Center and
the Ebola crisis among other issues.  Spent 2 hours getting interviewed.
Had telephone conference with Aftab Ansari (Emory) who has been doing the NHP 
studies with a4B7 in collaboration with us (Jim Arthos, Claudia Cicala, and me).   The 
data are amazing for a potential “cure”.   Cliff quite impressed.   I will lead a clinical 
study of anti-a4B7 antibody in HIV patients treated with ART and undetectable viral load 
to then D/C ART and see if the anti-a4B7 antibody blocks viral rebound.  Am making 
connections with Takeda Pharmaceuticals (who own the antibody).   Mike Sneller and to 
some extent in a learning capacity, Kat Clarridge will execute the clinical trial.  More 
later.   This might be the real thing.   We discovered the antibody and did all the 
subsequent studies over the past 7 years and most recently in the NHP in collaboration 
with Tab Ansari.   Now others, Nelson Michael (Army) and Elena Martinelli (former 
fellow of mine and now in NYC) also want to do a clinical study.   Only limited amount 
of antibody.   I clearly have first right for reasons given above.

Was supposed to go to Laura Grady’s wedding in Charleston, SC.
Has historic “Joaquin” Hurricane that gave massive floods (18 inches of rain).   I 
cancelled but Chris went.   The wedding was supposed to take place on a beach; however, 
this was impossible and so was moved to a mega-Church.   Lucky that I decided not to 
go.

Went to MIT in Boston to take part in an event called “SOLVE” aimed at
addressing and solving health problem throughout the world and domestically.   Phil 
Sharpe invited me and Susan Hockfield (former president of MIT) chaired the panel.   On 
my panel was Kiran Mazumdar (India), David Meeker (Genzyme), Mark McClellan 
(Brookings).   At lunch at “The Catalyst” preceding the Panel, Rick Klausner and other 
notables were there.   Good time.
Got to Boston early and had coffee with Jennifer and saw her apartment in Sommerville 
for the first time.   Beautiful place.   Also, wonderful to see Lucca who was very, very 
happy to see me.
Emerging problems with GSK over what adjuvant to use in the P5 HIV vaccine study in 
South Africa.  They bought out Novartis who used MF59 (our original agreement).   
However, now that GSK has the protein (we paid for it) they want to do the study with 
their adjuvant (ASO1B).   More later.   I may have to meet with GSK chief, Moncef 
Slaoui to settle this.

Senate Appropriations Subcommittee meeting.   I was not invited as a
witness.   Very strange.   Suspicion of Jack Whitescarver (I had dinner with him last 
night) and AIDS activists is that either Senator Cassidy or Francis himself did not want 
me there since I defend the AIDS budget so well and Cassidy keeps talking about cutting 
it.   Francis clearly wants to placate both Dems and GOP since he wants to stay as NIH 
Director after the elections (2016).  Francis says I was not invited since the Senators said

Gave interview to Reid Wilson who is writing a book on lessons learned
from Ebola.

Continue to work with Doug Brooks at NAPO, Kat Oakar, Amy Lansky
Knowlton on getting the program going with Valerie Jarrett’s help to end the AIDS 
epidemic in selected cities (SF, DC, Baltimore. Oakland, Atlanta).   Valerie is 
enthusiastic; however, she has made it clear that there is no new money for this project.   
We need to figure out a way to jump-start it with help of private organizations/ Cities/ 
States.   At my suggestion we are also involving Jono Mermin (CDC) and Laura Cheever 
(HRSA).   Had telepnone call with all of these today including Hilary Marston who has 
been very helpful to me on this.   Also, I have consulted with Mark Dybul, Debbie Birx 
and Paul Farmer in this overlap with my efforst to help Agnes Binagwaho to do the same 
in Rwanda.
Interesting conversation with Debbie Birx on Oct. 8 and she gave some caveats about 
Agnes as did Mark Dybul on a call on Sept. 18.   They are saying that Agnes is using 
PEPFAR and Global Fund money to build up her health systems and is getting already 2x 
more per HIV case than any other Southern African country.   They are very wary of 
giving her any more money.   I hope that she is not “playing” me to help her get more 
when others have refused for good reason.   I will keep an open mind.

Call with Mark Harrington who is concerned about Senator Cassidy’s
attack on the AIDS budget at the recent Senate Appropriations subcommittee Hearing.   
Also, he definitely gets it and is suspicious why I was not asked to testify.   He suspects 
that either Francis or the senators did not want my articulate voice  advocating for AIDS.
Went to book party/receiption for Jay Winik and his new book “1944 – FDR and the 
Year that Changed History” at Hay Adams Rooftop.  Party given by Catherine and 
Wayne Reynolds and Rick Atkinson.  The entire DC “A” list was there.   Had nice 
conversation with Rick about how my book is coming.   As usual, he was very 
encouraging of me.   Many friends there – Nino Scalia; Fred Hiatt; Sen. Blount; Jane and 
Calvin Cafritz; saw Jan Donaldson for first time in a couple of years after her divorce 
from Sam; Lloyd Hand; Ruth Marcus; Howard Fineman (very complimentary to me); 
many others.   Usual terrific time.
Had leadership Forum today and afterwards Francis Collins met with me and several 
other Institute Directors to discuss the Senate version of the House 21st Century Cures 
Bill. Sen. Lamar Alexander (Chair of the Senate HELP Committee) wants his own legacy 
and so wants to put some mandatory funding for the NIH; however, he wants the money 
to be earmarked. This is an authorization bill and not an appropriations bill and so I 
believe this is an example of the authorizers wanting to make their own legacy by 
encroaching upon the appropriators’s turf. I am very much against earmarked money. I 
suggested to Francis that he insist in his negotiations with Sen. Alexander that they put 
into the bill a provision for some proportion of the money to go to investigator-initiated 
grants. Here again, Francis is pushing the agenda of “precision medicine” which is

Received nice written letter from Michel Sidibe congratulating me for
doing the science that has helped us get to 15 million people receiving ARVs ahead of 
schedule.

Went to Yale School of Public Health (SPH) and received the Centennial
C.E.P. Winslow Medal and delivered the Award lecture.   The Winslow Medal is the 
highest honor bestowed by the Yale SPH.   My lecture on “Ending the HIV/AIDS 
Pandemic:   An Achievable Goal”.   They gave me a prolonged standing ovation.   Yale 
people tell me that is the first time in memory that anyone has ever received a standing 
ovation in that venue.  Enjoyed very much meeting with and having dinner (ROIA 
Restaurant in Downtown New Haven)) with the faculty, pre-and post-docs.   I was 
particularly struck by Alison Galvani a mathematical modeler epidemiologist who has 
written major papers on influenza, HIV and Ebola.   She is a 38 year old named Chair 
Professor of Epidemiology at Yale.   She looks like she is 18 years old.   Real genius and 
very nice.

Few more Ebola infections in Guinea.   Again and amazingly, MSF
wants us to give them ZMAPP to administer to patients outside of the RCT.  We cannot 
do this since we have been randomizing according to protocol all of our 65 patients 
including .   MSF refuses to participate in an RCT.   They are being in 
my mind unacceptably paternalistic by not giving the patient the choice of going on a 
trial or not.   They are trying to play super-ethical by giving drug to everyone, and that in 
my mind can even border on unethical since we still do not know whether the drug works 
or not or is harmful.

Met with Cuban ministers of health in 7A-24.  See WORD
attachment for the names of the delegates. Hopefully, this will be a first step in 
developing collaborations with the Cubans.
Cuban Delegation 
Bios and Institutions B

Appeared on WTOP Radio to discuss recent finding of statins decreasing
the immune response to influenza vaccine among elderly (>65 years old).

Was the Keynote Speaker together with Michel Sidibe (UNAIDS) at a
White House Conference on “U.S. Fast-track Cities and the National HIV/AIDS Strategy 
Meeting” hosted by Doug Brooks and ONAP.  Went very well.    
 
Off to NYC today to receive the “AID for AIDS” award tonight at Cipriani Restaurant 
(25 Broadway).  Invited by Bill Haseltine. 
Had good time at the event tonight.  Interesting crowd of mostly Hispanic-based AIDS 
advocates.   Bill Haseltine’s 3rd wife is lovely (Maria-Eugenia).   Got standing ovation 
after Bill presented the award to me.   At the event, had long conversation with  Nelson 
Cruz (Seattle Mariners) who wanted very much to meet me.   Tony Danza was there 
presenting award to Danny Pintauro.

entries.content:
Returned from NYC and was part of panel at the Dirksen Senate Office
Building.  Panel was Sens. Ed Markey, Bob Corker, Ben Cardin and Chris Coons; UN 
Deputy Secretary Ggeneral Jan Eliasson; Congressmen Barbara Lee and Jim Himes; 
Michel Sidibe and Fortunata Kasege and Deb Birx.
In the evening, filmed a segment for the upcoming series on “The Eighties” produced by 
Tom Hanks for HBO.

Participated in a “Bipartisan Policy Center” panel discussion on PEPFAR
held at the Newseum.   Program introduced by former Sens. Frist and Daschle.   My 
panel was chaired by Mike Gerson and Debbie Birx and former Finance Minister of 
Rwanda were on Panel.   Good program.

Had dinner with Danny and Chris Hultzen at American Tap Room in
Bethesda.   Becoming a tradition now in our 3rd year.   Caught up on Danny’s progress.   
He returns to Spring Training in January in Phoenix.   This is last of his option years and 
so he either makes the team (MLB) or he gets waived.   We discussed possibility of his 
becoming a relief pitcher since his arm gets fatigued after 50 to 60 pitches. What a great 
young man!   I really hope that he makes it and fulfills his dream since I knew him as a 
13 year old.
After dinner with the Hultzen’s,  I went with Chris to Georgetown to the Dog Tag Bakery  
upon invitation of Susan Axelrod.  She insisted that I come even if I was late.   There was 
a fund-raiser/reception/dinner for the CURE Epilepsy Foundation.   Paul Simon was the 
guest of honor.   He sang some of his hits (we did not get there in time to hear them); 
however, Chris and I had a wonderful 30 minute conversation with Paul.   Susan and 
David Axelrod were extremely generous in giving us seats on either side of Paul.   I was 
somewhat embarrassed since we walked in on them in the middle of their meal (they had 
just finished appetizers).  Paul and Chris and I spoke about his career, his children (he 
was very proud that his son had just been admitted (early decision) to Brown, and his 
philosophy about the political situation (he had just had lunch today with Bernie 
Sanders).   Apparently, Susan had told Paul all about me and he was very anxious to meet 
me.   He is truly a gentleman and a very modest and warm individual.   Great to meet 
him.   Also at the dinner were Sylvia Burwell, Valerie Jarrett, Senator Al Franken, Lisa 
Monaco among others.   Great evening!

Had dinner at the Home  of the French
Ambassador to the USA Gerard Araud.   Dinner in honor of Dr. Christian Brechot, the 
President of the Institut Pasteur.   Elegant affair.   Went with Chris.   All the many French 
there were excited to see me there.   They all remarked about seeing me on TV all the 
time, etc.

Horrible terrorist attacks in Paris by ISIS killing more than 125 people.
Bomb in soccer stadium where the President of France was watching the game (only few 
after approval from his upper management. We will put together a three page concept 
sheet for them to present to their upper management..

was called to the EEOB by Chris Kirchhoff to review a 55 page lessons
learned document that was put together by the National Security Council. It took me over 
two hours to review in Room 340 of the EEOB.  It was a pretty good document; however, 
they got some facts incorrect particularly related to the NIH PREVAIL 1 vaccine trial. I 
corrected this and also suggested that they put a statement in the document saying that the 
NIH should be the lead agency in the performance of research during outbreaks such as 
Ebola. I did this because of the difficulty we had when CDC decided to also do a vaccine 
trial in Sierra Leone.

Big day today.  It is World AIDS Day. Several important things happened
today. I went to the White House, and as has been the case over the past several years I 
was asked by ONAP director Doug Brooks to give the main address at the ceremony in 
the South Court auditorium of  EEOB. I gave a talk entitled “Ending the HIV/AIDS 
Pandemic: Follow the Science”. It was extremely well received and many members in the 
audience asked to have selfies taken with me. Also, on this day the Commentary that I 
wrote with Hillary Marston came out in the New England Journal of Medicine. In 
addition, a blog that Chris Beyrer and I wrote for the CNN blog also came out today. In 
addition, the Huffington Post wrote a very complementary blog on my TEDMED talk. 
Prior to the meeting in the South Court Auditorium, Doug Brooks and I together with 
Carl Dieffenbach, Laura Cheever, Jono Mermin, Heather Hauck, Eugene McCray, Amy 
Knowlton-Lansky, met in the West Wing office with Cecilia Munoz (Director of the 
White House Domestic Policy Council)  to discuss our test and link initiative that we 
(Doug Brooks and us) are putting together for five cities (San Francisco, Oakland, 
Baltimore, Washington DC, and Atlanta).  Cecilia was very encouraging; however, as 
expected there would be no new money for this initiative. All in all it was a very good 
day.
“VICE” did a show on HBO about HIV/AIDS for WAD and even though I was taped for 
over an hour, they did not show a single second of me.  The producer later that evening 
wrote a note to Patty and apologized, saying they just did not have enough time.   
However, the show was terrible.   They spent a lot of time on the “cure” of Tim Brown 
and on vaccine development in Seattle at the Hutch.   They also made it seem that Bono 
was the main person in developing PEPFAR with President Bush.    They could not have 
done a worse job.  Courtney wrote a note to the sub-producer expressing surprise and 
consternation that I was left out.   Her boss, Shawn Smith called Courtney and profusely 
apologized saying that my general comments on the history of AIDS were extremely 
eloquent; however, when they put the show together, they did not fit well with the 
direction of the specific points that they wanted to make about cure and vaccine.   He was 
mortified that they may have offended us.   Oh well…..

Had a wonderful dinner this evening at the home of David and Katherine
Bradley at    Dinner was in honor of Susan Desmond-Hellman, 
the new CEO of the Gates Foundation.   David is the CEO of The Atlantic Media 
Company, which owns The Atlantic, National Journal and Government Executive.   
Unfortunately, bad weather (fog) prevented Susan from coming from NYC to DC.  And 
so we had the dinner anyway and had great conversation and discussion of everything 
from Global Health (AIDS, by me), Presidential election in 2016, minority issues, ISIS, 
Syrian refugees, etc.   Present at the dinner were: James Bennet (Editor-in-Chief of the 
Atlantic), Ruth Marcus (Washington Post), Jane Mayer  (New Yorker), John Holdren 
(OSTP), Jarl Mohn (NPR), Michel Norris (NPR), Raj Shah (former USAID), Fred Hiatt 
(Washington Post), Helene Cooper (New York Times), Ruth Sherlock (The Telegraph), 
Sen Joe Donnelly (D-IN), Leon Wieseltier (Brookings/The Atlantic), Amanda Ripley 
(author, Time, The Atlantic).

Went to NAS on 21st Street, NW and presented my “vision” about where
we should go with biodefense and emerging microbe research.   John Holdren was 
present and was David Relman and others.   My take was to develop generic platforms 
and broad spectrum diagnostics and therapies and NOT concentrate of chasing individual 
agents and stockpiling for them.

Went to Atlanta to deliver one of the Opening Keynotes at the CDC-
organized National HIV Prevention Conference at the Atlanta Hyatt on peachtree.   
Spoke on “Ending the HIV/AIDS Pandemic:   Follow the Science”.   Three thousand 
people in the audience, many are community workers.   Very well received.   Also on 
program was Jono Mermin (Moderator), Doug Brooks (ONAP), Mindy Fullilove 
(Columbia), Eugene McCray (CDC).
We are organizing the a4B7 concept sheet that we will send to Takeda to get upper 
management approval for our proposed clinical trial.   Working with Cliff lane, Mike 
Sneller, Tae-Wook Chun, and Kat Clarridge.

Interviewed by GQ Magazine for a supposed “profile” on me.   I suspect
that the theme will be my clash with Senator Cassidy about AIDS research.   We shall see 
how it turns out.

Another fabulous dinner hosted by Catherine and Wayne Reynolds at the
Jefferson Hotel to honor Robert S. Langer of MIT (amazing inventor of medical devices, 
i.e. implantable birth control).  Attending were:  Tom Dashle and wife; Chris and 
Lorraine Wallace; Peter Agre; Rita Braver (CBS-Bob Barnett’s wife)    ; Fred and 
Margaret (Shapiro) Hiatt; Francis and Diane (Baker) Collins; Steve and Alice Rosenberg; 
Sen. Thad Cochrane and wife.
    Discussion was wide-ranging, a lot on the recent craziness of Donald Trump saying 
that we should not allow Muslims into the USA.
Truly, it was a 
memorable evening. I do hope that Chris and I will be able to maintain this friendship 
with Sebastian and Stephanie.

Another interesting entertainment evening.   John Salamone
formerly of NIAF got Chris and I tickets to the Verizon center to see an Andrea Bocelli 
concert.   We got to meet Bocelli at a private reception afterwards.   Several luminaries 
there – General James Jones; former Senator Chris Dodd (now president of Motion 
Pictures Corporation of America).

Had breakfast with Peggy Hamburg at the Daily Grill in the Bethesda
Hyatt.   She is recently retired as Commissioner of FDA.   Met for “career 
advice/discussion”.   She is trying to figure out what she wants to do next.
Also, today was the Kinyoun Lecture with Debbie Birx (Ambassador of PEPFAR).   
Debbie told me some disturbing things about the implementation of programs in Southern 
Africa – drug stock-outs; only giving drug supply 1 month at a time and so some people 
are skipping some months.   Also, considerable corruption.   She may be exaggerating for 
effect.

Had “secret” teleconference in the Natcher Building SCIF connected
with White House (Amy Pope – Ron Klain successor) + Nicki Lurie, Leslie Dasch, 
USAID people and also connected to CDC with Tom Frieden.   Purpose was to go over 
the status of the situation in West Africa regarding Ebola.   Nothing new.   Last case was 
in Liberia – unexplained – very likely woman who was sub-clinically infected got 
pregnant and her virus resurged giving her minimal sxs; however, she apparently infected 
her husband and sons, or they infected each other after one of them got infected from 
mother.

Important meeting in person (my office) and by teleconference with the
members of P5 to discuss moving forward with trial in RSA.   Present in my office – 
Emilio Emini (BMGF), Larry Corey, Nina Russell (BMGF), Carl Dieffenbach, Rip Balou 
(GSK), John Siever (Sanofi), Hilary Marston, and GSK person over the phone 
(Marguerite).   We agreed on plan forward.  Start the ALVAC + protein + MF59 adjuvant 
in October, 2016.   Then do bridge study to see if it is better to use ASO1b adjuvant.

I had invited Bono to give the Barmes lecture at NIH on behalf of francis
Collins.   I just received this nice e-mail from him:
From: PDH @invisible.ie] 
Sent: Sunday, December 20, 2015 8:23 PM
To: Fauci, Anthony (NIH/NIAID) [E]
Cc: Collins, Francis (NIH/OD) [E]; Allison Biggs
Subject: Re: Note from Tony Fauci
Tony, my humblest apologies for not replying to your very attractive invitation to speak 
at NIH…it really does sound like my cup of tea but as you probably picked up, these days 
more and more of my time and tea drinking belongs to the band so hardly have room for 
ONE/(RED) and other-committed activities. Can’t get to the fun stuff as much although i 
will say ONE and (RED) give me extraordinary pleasure…(RED) now $350m to the 
Global Fund and ONE fighting in every capital for the stuff you and i both believe 
in…2016 doesn’t look like it’s going to be a lot easier….we are recording a new album 
and then on the road again… I’ve asked Allison to keep an eye on my schedule and we’ll 
let you know if anything looks possible.  Please give my best to your family.  That visit to 
your house was thirteen years ago… the number of people on ARVs has grown 15 fold 
since then.  What did you put in that pasta.  Happy Christmas and love to Christine and 
the kids…
B
On Oct 28, 2015, at 2:05 PM, Fauci, Anthony (NIH/NIAID) [E] 
<
AFAUCI@niaid.nih.gov> wrote:
Bono:
   Hope that all is well with you.  I had sent the below e-mail to you in August and found out very 
recently that I did not have the best e-mail address to reach you.  Tom Hart just provided for me 
the one that I am using now.   Please take a look at my attached letter  to you.  
Warm regards,
Tony
 
From: Fauci, Anthony (NIH/NIAID) [E] 
Sent: Friday, August 28, 2015 2:26 PM
To: @elevation.com'
Cc: Collins, Francis (NIH/OD) [E]
Subject: Note from Tony Fauci
 
Hi Bono:
   Warm greetings to you from Bethesda.  Hope that you are well.  Please see my attached note.
Best regards,
Tony

National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases

sender's own and not expressly made on behalf of the NIAID by one of its representatives

Had terrific Christmas holiday with my 3 daughters visiting with their
dogs Sammy and Lucca.  Did the usual Christmas Eve/birthday dinner over my sister 
Denise’s house.   Am struck by the fact that I am now 75 years old.   Very strange feeling 
since I do not feel at all like what I thought 75 years old would be from my perceptions 
over the years regarding 75 year old men.  I feel like I am a wise and experienced and 
accomplished 40 year old.
     Over the holidays, I appeard on PBS NewsHour in a pre-taped segment on Ebola.   
Quite a good segment showing me in PPE.   Also appeared in a taped segment on CBS 
This Morning speaking on “The Common Cold”.

Spent a week in Cabo, Mexico with the every 3.5 year meeting
of the HPIM Editorial Board.   Chris came down for 5 days and Ali was there for 3 days.   
Wonderful place!    Great meeting.   Weather was wonderful, hotel spectacular (Cabo 
Azul).   Superb food – surprisingly, I ate almost everything – mostly broiled fish (right 
out of the water).   Went deep sea fishing with Dennis Kasper; did not catch fish, but saw 
many, many whales.   Too bad Chris had already left for home since she really wanted to 
see whales.

Back in action.   Catching up with plenty to do.   Zika virus and
accompanying micrencephaly is rapidly spreading in Brazil with >3000 of 
microencephaly.   I am writing a Perspective (hopefully to NEJM) with David Morens.

Very good past few days.   Upon the invitation of Fred Hiatt (Editor of
the Editorial Page of the Washington Post) I wrote an Opinion Piece for the Post.   I 
wrote it on my last day in Cabo and submitted it this past week.   They accepted it within 
15 minutes of my submission.   It appeared in today’s Sunday Post (01-10-2015).   Fred 
got interested in it related to the dinner we both attended over David Bradley’s home (see 
above) and spoke to the attendees at the dinner about ending the HIV/AIDS Pandemic.
      Also, the NEJM accepted my Perspective on Zika Virus 2 days after submission!.   It 
will appeared Online next week.    Not a bad week.

Zika situation heating up!   325 cases this week in Brazil of
microcephaly!!!   My picture was in today’s issue of USA Today related to my NEJM 
article (see above).   Interesting that yesterday HHS would not allow us (NIAID) to do a 
press statement associated with my NEJM paper.   Bill Hall approved it and then Leslie 
Dach overturned him and said no!!!   I strongly suspect that the CDC complained that I 
was talking about Zika when they had “the lead” and they pressured him to over-rule Bill.   
They allow me to do TV, but they did not want the media Announcement to go out.   
Here we go again.   They are idiots.   They feel that the press would get confused since 
the CDC also made an announcement today that they demonstrated by PCR Zika in the 
brains of 2 miscarriages and 2 live births who died soon after.   HHS and CDC apparently 
feel that the press cannot distinguish between a scholarly article in NEJM and an 
announcement about autopsy findings.
     In any event, the press roles in.  I did NBC Nightly News tonight; CNN Blog, Voice 
of America and some science press related to my article.

Took great trip to Monrovia, Liberia with Cliff Lane.   We site visited
the clinics and facilities that cliff has been working with over the past more than one 
year.   We visited Redemption Hospital and JFK Hospital where we renovated the clinics.  
Also went to LIBR (Liberian Institute for Biomedical Research).   Visited the U.S. 
Embassy and met with Ambassador Mark Boulware and DCM Sheila Parkman.   Mark 
had just started 5 weeks ago; however, Sheila was great and was extremely helpful to 
Cliff throughout the conduct of the PREVAIL trials (Partnership for Research on Ebola 
in Liberia).   PREVAIL 1 was the vaccine trials; PREVAIL 2 was the ZMapp trial and 
PREVAIL 3 is the survivor study.  
     I also visited the CDC in the location of the embassy. I met with the CDC staff who 
had been mostly helpful to Cliff. Most of all I interacted with the staff that Cliff had put 
together over the past year. They were extremely excited to see me and I had an 
absolutely wonderful time interacting with them. I was deeply impressed with how run 
down the entire city of Monrovia was. I imagine the rest of the country is no better. It 
seemed that the homes were just one shack and shantytown type residents that were in 
extraordinary ill repair. I did not see any part of the city that looked like it was in good 
shape despite the fact that we drove around for hours from place to place. The 
Redemption Hospital which we have renovated was a broken down and falling apart 
structure. Apart from our renovated rooms it looked like a condemned building. I learned 
that the country still has not recovered from the Civil War which ended in 2003. There 
were many unfinished buildings that was started before the war and that just stopped 
during and after the war. This is a country that is in serious trouble. However I am told 
that they are making great strides and they are much better than what they were a couple 
of years ago. While we were in Liberia there was a secondary case of Ebola in a contact 
of the 22-year-old woman who died about 10 days ago. The trip was strenuous, but I did 
very well throughout.
    Zika virus situation is continuing to heat up. The CDC came out with 
recommendations for pregnant women who might be traveling to the involved regions. 
Unfortunately, they are a bit confusing since there is no real definitive and highly specific 
serological test that distinguishes Zika from dengue and other flaviviruses. The press 
interest continues and I will be on CNN tomorrow (Jan. 21) commenting on the 
progression of the outbreak and the disturbing number (now 3500) cases of 
microcephaly.

More attention to Zika situation.   Did CNN New Day this AM and BBC
taped for 5:00 PM slot and long segment for Brazilian TV – “TV Globo – News”.   Also, 
interview with Time Magazine.
Major Blizzard snow storm coming to DC tomorrow (Friday) and Saturday.

the situation with Zika virus is intensifying as the epidemic is beginning
to explode in South America and the Caribbean, particularly in the North Eastern section 
of Brazil (Recife). It is estimated that there are over 1 million cases of Zika virus 
infection in Brazil and there has been more than a 20 fold increase in incidence of 
microcephaly in infants born of mothers infected during pregnancy. This is now gaining 
worldwide attention and I am being called upon more and more by the press to comment 
on the disease itself as well as on the preparation of NIH for the possibility that this will 
appear in the United States. The relationship between Zika infection in pregnant women 
and microcephaly in the fetus/infant is still an “association” and cause-effect has not yet 
been definitively established.   I keep making that point.  Of note, the CDC has now listed 
22 countries where there is local transmission of Zika. These countries are in South 
America and the Caribbean. There is local transmission in Puerto Rico and there has been 
the case in the U.S. Virgin Islands. The CDC has put out guidelines that women who are 
pregnant, or plan to be pregnant should avoid travel to the designated countries until the 
situation gets clarified. They have also put out guidelines of what pregnant women who 
have been to the area and who may or may not have been infected should do.   Also, a 
single case of very likely sexual transmission of Zika has occurred, which really 
complicates the issue for men who go to the region and return regarding the possibility 
that they may transmit the infection to their wives at home whom may be pregnant or 
about to be pregnant.   In fact, the Brits will announce next week that they recommend 
that men who travel to the region use condoms for 1 month following return home.   
Also, a possible case of transmission through blood transfusion which led FDA next 
week to issue self-deferral guidelines for people travelling to the region similar to the 
situation with malaria for people who have traveled to malaria zones.

BEGINNING OF AN AMAZING WEEK!!!.  I have been informed
that there will be a meeting with the POTUS tomorrow in the Situation Room of the 
White House. Press interest continues and I have done much print press (NY Times, 
Washington Post, Reuters, AP, etc.  as well as BBC radio and others.

appeared on the Diane Rehm Show with Maggie Fox (NBC) as the other
guest in the studio and Scott Weaver calling in. Also did NPR radio with Rob Stein and 
multiple  print media. Big event of the day was a one hour and 40 min. meeting with 
President Obama in the Situation Room of the White House (4:00 PM to 5:45 PM)  to 
discuss the overall strategy to address the threat of Zika to the United States and our 
response to helping out in the Caribbean and South America. The agenda of the meeting 
was a dual presentation first by Tom Frieden through video link from Geneva where he 
was attending a WHO conference. I was in the Situation Room as the second part of the 
presentation concerning the research response to the outbreak. Present in the room among 
others were: Vice President Biden, Denis McDonough (Chief of Staff to the President), 
Lisa Monaco (head of NSC), Susan Rice, Sylvia Burwell, Shaun Donovon (Director - 
OMB), Valerie Jarrett, Gayle Smith (USAID Director), Heather Higginbottom (Deputy - 
USAID), Gina McCarthy (Director EPA), Jeff Zients (Economic Advisor), John Holdren 
(Science Advisor) .  President Obama clearly wants to stay ahead of the situation and 
tasked us to come up with an immediate as well as a broad plan to address not only the 
current situation but future situations. He turned to me multiple times during the meeting 
for my opinion. When he spoke about addressing the immediate issue, Denis McDonough 
noticed that I was a bit uncomfortable. After the meeting, Denis stayed on and came over 
to me and told me that he has known me a long time (he was a staffer for Senator 
Daschle) and knows my body language. He picked up that there was something not 
completely right with my reaction to the President. In fact, I was concerned that when the 
President spoke about what he wanted to do, it was a little too focused on developing 
vaccines for Zika, dengue, and Chikungunya, as opposed to the broader plan that I 
thought he would want us to formulate. On the way out of the White House, Sylvia 
Burwell suggested that she connect Denis and me by e-mail so that we can chat by phone 
and clarify just what I felt should be done and how that aligned with what the President 
wanted.
   I came back to the NIH and set up a meeting with both intramural and extramural that 
might be involved in our response making it clear that this is an emergent situation and 
we have to put on a full-court press in doing what we do in the arena of research and 
development of countermeasures.
    Subsequent to the meeting with Obama, there is now a press fury about the situation. I 
have been given open clearance to talk to the press similar to what I did with Ebola. In 
fact during the meeting at the White House, Lisa Monaco and the President explicitly 
indicated that they wanted me on TV giving as much outreach and clarification and 
calming of the public with the evidence-based facts as possible.
I have copied below the Summary of the January 26, 2016 meeting:

And so the media blitz begins. I will list just some of the important
appearances in addition to the countless print press interviews. I appeared this morning 
on CNN new day, ABC nightly news, CNN with Jake Tapper.

Am rapidly mobilizing my staff to respond with the research plan. I have
made Hilary Marston the point person since already the workflow is becoming very 
intense. I am mobilizing John Mascola to pursue the DNA vaccine approach that leads to 
viral like particles, which was the one that we successfully used to bring a West Nile 
Virus vaccine into phase 1 trials several years ago. We did not take it any further since 
we could not find a pharmaceutical partner. I do not anticipate that we will have a 
problem finding partners because of the intense interest in this right now. In addition, we 
are putting out funding opportunity announcements to get the research community 
involved. We are moving quickly by supplementing already existing grants on dengue 
and other flaviviruses, both with American investigators and our Brazilian colleagues.
    Margaret Chan, director of WHO, has now made an announcement that Zika is a 
rapidly expanding pandemic that would involve "the Americas", as well as all of Africa, 
Asia, and southern Europe. She is clearly covering her ass because of the very slow and 
inadequate response of WHO to the Ebola outbreak. This has led to a misunderstanding 
that they would inevitably be a major local outbreak in the United States of America. I 
have been spending almost all of my time now with the press trying to give a calm 
evidence-based assessment of what is going on. For example, today I appeared on CBS 
Morning Show with Norah O’Donnell, Charlie Rose and Gayle King, Fox Channel 5 TV, 
WTOP radio, NBC Nightly News, CBS Nightly News, BBC radio, PBS NewsHour with 
Judy Woodruff, Good Morning America with George Stephanopoulos, Charlie Rose - 
Bloomberg, among others.
     In addition, I got a call from my friend from the Ebola situation, Ron Klain. Ron is 
working on Hillary Clinton's campaign and called saying that Hillary asked him to ask 
me if I would be comfortable with briefing her staff on Zika. This made me quite 
uncomfortable since as a government worker I should not get involved at all in any 
political campaigns. Ron agreed with me that it would be a good idea for me not to do 
this unless I did it for every one of the candidates. I mentioned to Ron that I was 
concerned that Hillary would be upset with me. Ron assured me that she completely 
understood my situation. Therefore, I will not brief them.

another amazing day!! Appeared on CNN new day and MSNBC Morning
Joe.  Then I went down to the Renaissance Hotel to appear at a longtime prearranged 
lunch at the Renaissance Hotel given by the Economic Club of Washington DC. This is 
chaired by my friend David Rubenstein, the CEO of the Carlyle group. David is also the 
President of the Kennedy Center. This is an event where he and I would get on stage after 
a luncheon and David would interview me about health issues in general. However, due 
to the furor of the Zika situation, there were dozens of reporters there and at least six 
television cameras recording the interview. We spent considerable time on Zika; 
however, we also discussed a number of other interesting health issues. The room was 
packed with a few hundred people, and the interview went extremely well. I am very 
impressed with David who is one of the great philanthropists of our time. For example, as 
a billionaire he gives away a couple of hundred million dollars per year. Most recently, 
he renovated the Washington Monument that was damaged by the recent earth quake. In 
addition he has renovated the Iwo Jima Memorial. He plans to soon do something with 
the Lincoln Memorial.
    Other press today included NPR Morning Edition.
     Another important event was the phone call that I had with Denis McDonough. 
Dennis explained to me that what the President really wants is to address this outbreak in 
the broadest sense in the context of what the effect of climate change, i.e. global 
warming, would have on our vulnerability to mosquito borne infections such as Zika, 
dengue and Chikungunya, among others. He wanted to develop a comprehensive plan but 
what we would do if years from now the southeastern part of the country becomes a 
semi-tropical region similar to Puerto Rico. Our response would involve everything from 
vector control to the development of vaccines for appropriate mosquito borne infections. 
Denis asked my opinion of how we could get this program started. I suggested that we 
get Sylvia Burwell involved in that she could utilize the office of the Assistant Sec. for 
Prevention and Response (ASPR). I e-mailed Sylvia and asked her to call me about this 
since Dennis is going to give this topic to Obama during their "daily walk" at the end of 
the day to bring up with Sylvia in his regular meeting with her that is scheduled for this 
coming Monday, February 1.  It looks like I am going to get involved in another broad 
public health issue at the level of the White House..
   In addition to all of this, Jim Kim, President of the World Bank called me asking for my 
advice and help in how the World Bank could help with the evolving Zika situation. He 
expressed the same concerned that he did with Ebola, i.e. that Margaret Chan and WHO 
as well as the people at PAHO are completely not up to the task of responding. He asked 
what I thought the most important thing to do right now. Once again, I emphasized that 
vector control is absolutely critical and that we have to put a full-court press on mosquito 
elimination and control in Brazil and other South American countries. 
Jim is very 
concerned that Brazil could experience an economic collapse particularly if the Olympic 
Games scheduled for this summer in Brazil are canceled because of Zika.  He feels that if 
Brazil collapses, Argentina will follow and all of South America would be in dire straits. 
I suggested to him that he contact Sylvia.

Had long telephone conversation with Sylvia (Saturday - I believe she
was at a soccer match with her child - maybe - noise in background).  I gave her a heads-
up for her meeting with the President on this Monday. Sylvia is a concerned that the 
President is putting too much emphasis on the effects of climate change and global 
warming due to the "Greek Chorus" of people in the White House led by John Holdren 
(Science Advisor) who keep pushing the climate change agenda. Sylvia feels they try to 
link it to health to give it more attention. She is showing wisdom and wants to make sure 
that the President understands that things like respiratory diseases spread by travel rather 
than by mosquitoes or other issues related to climate change are much more important

on 19th Street, NW.   To be shown on NYC TV.
Gave lecture on Zika to big crowd at the Cosmos Club.   Organization was EcoHealth

Went to National Press Club to do a 1-on-1 interview on Zika in front
of audience brought together by Scientific American.  
Did WTOP interview on recent delineation of the molecular structure of Zika virion.
Spoke for 1 hour with Laura Friedel and Alex Keenan, Clerks of the Senate Labor HHS 
Appropriations Subcommittee.  Good interchange.

Did interview on CNN with Jake Tapper – “The Lead” on the CDC
Summit that took place today in Atlanta.   It was designed to coordinate the responses of 
the State and Local Health authorities in the event of a Zika outbreak in the USA.   Asked 
for  state-wide action plan for each state and a state coordinator for each state.
Nice farewell party for Doug Brooks at the home of Ernest Hopkins at  
.   Many of the AIDS group were there wishing him well as he leaves to work as the 
community person for Gilead Sciences.    Doug is a good person.

Most activity still centered around Zika.  USG concerned about what
will happen aas we enter the mosquito season in the spring/summer here in the 
continental USA.   Have been on NBC local TV news with Doreen Gentzler for past 2 
evenings (April 4-5).

Did a mock drill on a fake Nipah patient in the Special Clinical Studies
Unit (SCSU) with the old Ebola team of nurses and personnel.   Entire thing filmed by 
the Discovery Channel that is doing a Special on the Clinical Center.   Well very well.

Went to San Francisco to give the 2016 Canada Gairdner Golbal Health
Award lecture at the 7th Annual Consortium of Universities for Global Health (CUGH).   
Arrived late afternoon and went to dinner at John’s Grill on 63 Ellis Street (Eric 
Goosby’s favorite place from his youth in SF).   At dinner was Paul Volberding, Molly 
Coy, Diane Havlir, Eric, John……,Minister of Health of Ethiopia  Kesetebirhan Admasu.   
Great dinner.

Gave the Gairdner Award lecture on “Ending the HIV/AIDS Pandemic:
An Achievable Goal”.   Standing ovation, many tweets.   Then did panel of Global Health 
and AIDS with Diane Havlir, Eric Goosby, and Peter Piot.   Then had Gairdner lunch at 
the 55 Parc Restauruat with John Dirks (Gairdner person), King Holmes, Peter Piot, 
Heidi Larson, Haile Debas, etc.
Then had dinner with Ali and 2 of her old Stanford classmates at Aperto restaurant on 
18th and Connecticut in Potrero Hill.   Great dinner.
Then took red-eye home.

Did major press briefing on Zika in the White House Press Room with
Anne Schuchat, hosted by Obama Press Secretary Josh Earnest.  Then Anne and I did sit 
down briefing with several reporters from varied state and local newspapers.

Much press associated with my appearance yesterday at the White
House Press room.   They focused on the issue of our needing the $1.9 billion supplement 
that Obama asked for.   Also, the issue of the more we learn about Zika, the worse it gets, 
particularly with the new information about the range of neurological problems:  few 
examples of press: WTOP radio; San Francisco KCBS Radio; Sirius XM radio; BBC 
radio; CNN International TV; all print newspapers including picture on front page of 
USA Today.

Continue intense press interest.  Today did: Good Morning America –
ABC with Robin Roberts; Fox and Friends TV; Diane Rehm Radio Show.
Also, presented briefing on Zika to the Ambassadors from foreign countries at the HHS 
auditorium.   Also presenting were Beth Bell (CDC), Lu Borio (FDA), Judy Garber 
(State).
Had teleconference with Amy Pope (coordinating Zika at White House) in Situation 
Room of White House (I was in the SCIF at HHS).

Kevin Griffis (Asst Secr. For Pubic Affairs at HHS) arranged for me to
brief by phone the Editors of the New York Times and the L.A. Times on Zika and the 
budget battle between the Congress and the Administration over the $1.9 billion 
supplement request.    It is becoming political in that media such as Jon LaPook at CBS is 
blasting the Republican Congress for not granting the supplemental request.   I am 
inadvertently getting involved in a political battle  since the Administration wants my 
public credibility to show how wrong the Republicans are in not granting the $1.9 billion 
Zika supplement.   In fact, on Sunday (April 17, 2016) I will appear on Fox News Sunday 
with Chris Wallace and on Face the Nation. To argue for the need for the supplement.

Delivered the Plenary Lecture at the Joint AAP/ASCI, ASPA meeting
in Chicago.   Came back same day.   Poignant moments when I ran into the old giants and 
heroes of Internal Medicine – Holly Smith and Don Seldin both of whom are looking old 
and frail.   That will be me years from now.

Appeared on Fox News Sunday with Chris Wallace and on Face the
Nation.  Went extremely well.   Following the appearances, all of the print media had me 
explaining why we need the $1.9 billion supplement that the POTUS had asked for.   My 
quotes about Zika (ex: likely that there will be local transmissions similar to dengue, etc.) 
dominated the print media as well as subsequent followups on TV on April 18/19.

Appeared on CNBC Squawk Box and Fox Local News regarding prior
appearances on Sunday Shows. 
Had the Annual BMGF/NIH workshop to discuss collaborations with the Gates people.   
Meeting held in Porter Building on a glorious sunny Monday.   Bill Gates was at the 
meeting for the entire morning.   We had some good discussions.

Battle ongoing between Dems and GOP regarding whether to fund the
$1.9 billion request from Obama for Zika supplement.   Apparently, my appearances on 
TV have “pushed” the GOP to give in a bit.   Now negotiating regarding how much of the 
request to grant.

I appeared on FOX News with Cavuto.
Had great meeting with the two CHAVI-IDs – Bart Haynes and Dennis Burton (also John 
Mascola present) to discuss the progress with the broadly neutralizing antibody and 
immunogen approach.   We are making progress in a complex area.
Had urgent call from Amy Pope at the NSC/EOP asking about the impact of what I 
would be able to do/not do if I got only $200 million of the $277 million slated for NIH.   
Apparently she just spoke with Denis McDonough and Denis told her to check with me 
since there is obviously a deal brewing between the WH and the GOP.   
Got animated call from Rosa DeLauro who is incensed that the Senate Dems and the WH 
are looking like they are “caving in” to the GOP in not insisting that we stick by our guns 
for the entire supplement.   She was angry and cursing at the WH and the Senate DEMS.   
Used the “F” bomb multiple times.   She is counting on me to stand my ground.

Lunch in the LBJ Room of the Capitol with Senate Dem Caucus.
Meeting with me, Sylvia Burwell, and Anne Schuchat (CDC) to discuss budget 
negotiations.  Went very well.   Obviously, the DEMs are pushing for all of the 
supplement; however, they are realistic and realize that they will have to settle for part, 
likely ~$1.1 billion.   Much praise by the senators regarding my years of service.   Those 
in particular who commented were: Mikulski, Feinstein, Boxer, Schumer, Reid, etc.

Did WTOP Radio with Mike Moss and Joan Jones on the NIH
influenza challenge study showing that protection is associated more with antibody to NA 
versus antibody to HA.
Also, appeared on Fox Business News TV

Gave a talk at the Marmon Hall of the Shakespeare Theater on 6th and F
St, NW to the Smithsonian Science and Engineering Festival.   Was actually an interview 
format on my experience with emerging infections.

Tension still tight between the GOP and Dems about the Zika
supplement request.   I was on the now weekly call with Amy Pope of the NSC via the 
SCIF in the Natcher Building with CDC, ASPR, White House, DoD, USAID, and State 
talking about Zika and doing our weekly update and planning session.
Went to a Nats game at Nats Stadium with Bob Seder.   Unfortunately it was very cold 
and threatening of rain.   Nats lost despite good showing by Gio Gonzales.  Nats did not 
get many hits.   Bob and I walked out (as usual) after the 5th inning.

Busy day.  Went to Humphrey Building to be with Sylvia Burwell when
she gave a teleconference Press briefing reporting on her trip to Puerto Rico to check out 
the Zika situation there.
Then had important meeting with Sen. Burr in his office in the Dirksen Building.  Also 
present were Nicki Lurie, Richard Hatchett (having taken over at BARDA for Robin 
Robinson), Annie Abramson (Burr’s chief staffer), Bob Kadlec (my old friend from 
BioShield days), Patty Conrad and Melinda Haskins.
Burr is upset about a few things.  First he is frustrated that he created BARDA and now 
every time there is a global health emergency, we ask for emergency funds.   I had to 
explain that BARDA is very successful in providing funds for countermeasures; however, 
the response to outbreaks involves more than producing and stockpiling 
vaccines/drugs/etc.   It also involved all the surveillance and public health work of CDC.  
Also, and importantly, all the work we do on pathogenesis and the high cost of clinical 
trials.   He got it.   However, he was also upset that the language of the supplement 
request tried to change the purpose of BARDA by stating that it should be used for any 
public health issue that poses a threat at the same time that the administration is actually 
cutting money from BARDA and trying to steal from the BioShield account.  
He was not upset with me at all and we still are good friends.   He is frustrated with the 
administration.
Along the lines of the Zika supplement “wars”, Nancy Pelosi called me in my office 
tonight and asked if I would go to the Congress on May 10 and explain the importance of 
our needing the Zika supplement.

First death due to Zika in Puerto Rico, related to severe
thrombocytopenia in a man in his 70s.
Press interest continues in the diseases and in the budget battles.   Did interview with a 
terrific person for radio and TV for BBC to air on May 5.   Also did NBC Nightly News 
and MSNBC with Chuck Todd  
Met with Paul Stoffels (J & J; Janssen) together with Emilio Emini, Larry Corey, Nina 
Russell, Carl D. and Mary Marovich to discuss the funding and governance and design of 
the upcoming HIV vaccine trial with the human Ad26 /MVA boost to take place in South 
Africa.   Good discussion.   Paul is an old friend.
 
Had dinner with Catherine and Wayne Reynolds at Chez Francois in Great Falls, VA.   
Guests included Chris Grady, Francis Collins, Mike Morell (former Acting Director, 
CIA), Mary Beth Morell, General James Jones, Diane Jones.   Many interesting 
conversations about Middle east, the Trump driven primaries, the likelihood or not of 
Hilary Clinton getting indicted for the e-mail situation.  General JamesJones telling me 
how disappointed he is in Obama for relinquishing USA leadership throughout the world, 
including in Ukraine and especially in the Middle East.   Mike Morell underscored this 
both essentially saying that Obama has been a foreign policy disaster.   Interesting since 
they both served in the Obama administration.

Annual typical and wonderful Garden Brunch at
given by Tammy Haddad, Hilary Rosen, Franco Nuschese et al.   Since I have been on a 
lot of TV/radio of late with regard to Zika (see above), I was readily recognized by many 
of the movie and TV stars.   Really good time meeting and having conversation with the 
usual DC people (Valerie Jarrett, Linda Douglas, Wolf Blitzer, etc) whom I always meet 
at these parties as well as Michael Kelly (Doug in “House of Cards”), Ian Kahn (AMC’s 
Washington’s Spies), Jaimie Alexander (NBC’s “Blindspot”).   Had great conversation 
with Ian Kahn who felt passionately that if today’s politicians would ask before they act - 
:What would George Washington have done?” we would have a better country.  Ian plays 
George Washington in a TV Series.  He wants to reach out to me after the weekend. Also, 
ran into Jim Sciutto and his wife and other Regis High School grads (somewhat of a 
multi-generational reunion).

NAS Annual meeting.   I defended dennis Kasper and Bart Haynes.
Kasper did  very well in discussion in section 44 (Microbiology); however, a few people 
in Section 43 (Immunology - Sasha Rudinsky and Emil Unanue) trashed Dennis for no 
apparent reason.  Bart did well in Section 43.

Did very successful briefing on Zika at PAHO of the PAHO country
“communicators”   Many press there including 12 TV cameras from all over the 
Americas.   Organized by Bill Hall from HHS.
