entries.content:
Did Hearst TV and Fox 5 News on Zika.   Went to NFID Dinner and
Awards night to present Maxwell Finland Award to Diane Griffin (Hopkins) whom I 
nominated.   Held at Bethesda Hyatt.
Zika still dominating the news.
Bad situation – Francis Collins notified John Gallin that he was essentially “fired” since 
the Red Team report recommended that NIH appoint a CEO to run the Clinical Center 
because of the issue brought up by the “investigation” by the team, i.e. inconsistent 
attention among some ICs for patient safety and FDA compliance with pharmacy and IV 
issues.   NIAID did great in the evaluation, but other ICs did not.   Francis is throwing 
John under the bus on this one. 
The Red Team led by Norman Augustine was called in by Francis to investigate the issue 
of the conditions (that came to light last May – 2015) in the CC Pharmacy with 
compounding  experimental drugs.   No patient was hurt but it was clear that in an 
attempt to service investigators, the pharmacy did not abide by strict GMP practices, 
particularly in the physical structure of the pharmacy modules.  Two vials were found 
with precipitate in them and the Pharmaceutical Development Branch was closed.   The 
FDA investigated and was not pleased at first with the response.   Meanwhile the “Red 
Team” did a broad look at the CC and found  a culture of caring more for research than 
for the patients (not at NIAID, but in other ICs).   One thing led to another and the 
recommendation was to appoint a CEO for the CC, which in effect eliminates John 
Gallin.   There is some truth in the inconsistencies in care among the ICs; however, John 
Gallin was never given the authority to do anything about it.   Yet, he is being blamed.   It 
is up to the ICs to demand excellence.   John is a bit at fault since he has been very 
passive in demanding (even though he did not have the authority) that the ICs do better.   
Francis is also at fault since he never gave the CC the resources to have a pharmacy or 
other facilities that are up to today’s standards.
NIH Record  New 
Oversight Coming to C     
`

Amazing weekend at Ohio State University for the Commencement
Address.   I spoke in the Ohio Stadium in front of 70,000 people!!.   My talk went 
extremely well.   There were initial tweets over the prior couple of weeks and write-ups 
in the school papers about “mixed feelings” among students that they got a “relatively 
unknown” personality to be commencement speaker instead of a celebrity comedian or 
movie star.   Last year they had Obama.   Some students said that they had looked me up 
and found that my accomplishments were amazing and they were interested in what I had 
to say.  Others expressed disappointment that I was not a celebrity.   That all changed 
after the address.   The enthusiasm for me was amazing.   All the tweets praised me as did 
the school newspapers.   I was mobbed as I left the stadium by hundreds of students and 
parents who want to shake my hand, touch me, take “selfies’ with me.    This continued at 
the airport where literally hundreds of people came up to me to congratulate and praise 
ny talk.   Amazing weekend!

Went to NYC for a DDCF Board meeting.   Got there early to do an
interview with the Editorial Board of BuzzFeed located on East 18th Street.   Beautiful 
sunny day.   I enjoyed walking around Union Square and then realized that I was near 
Larry Kramer’s apartment on , right near Washington Square Park.   I 
spontaneously dropped in on him (Apartment ) and had a great chat.   He was thrilled 
that I visited him.
Had pre-brief with Sylvia Burwell by phone in preparation for our lunch meeting 
tomorrow with the Editorial Board of the Washington Post.   Sylvia called me back 
afterwards and expressed concern about the CDC was handling the Zika issue.   Sylvia 
does not trust their judgment and competence based on her experience with Ebola.
  
Did interview on NPR – “Morning Edition” with Renee Montagne on Zika to be aired 
tomorrow.

Article came out in Washington Post by Lena Sun describing on the Red
Team’s report.   Very damaging to NIH.   NIH community vey angry with Francis 
Collins for essentially allowing this in order to cover his ass.   Gallin is the sacrificial 
lamb.   Francis announced that the NIH will have  CEO, COO and CMO and the Gallin 
will have to step down, i.e. John was fired.
Did great on camera interview on Facebook and Online for USA Today with senior editor 
Susan Paige.
Continued back and forth in Congress regarding the $1.8 billion request for Zika.   I will 
testify tomorrow before the House in a special briefing areranged by Nancy Pelosi.

My picture was in USA Today and I was prominently mentioned in a
Washington Post Editorial and a NY Times Editorial.   Anne Schuchat, Mitch Landrieu 
(Mayor of New Orleans) and I briefed the Democratic Steering Group for Zika in The 
Capitol Visitors Center at 1:00 PM<.   Chaired by Pelosi with Nita Lowy, Rosa DeLauro, 
etc.   35 Members present.   Great hearing.   Love fest for me by my old friends (Pelosi et 
al).   Did TV interview for the ABC World News Tonight.
Francis Collins wants my help in trying to fashion something for John within the Clinical 
Center that would be acceptable to him.   Francis obviously realizes the unpopularity of 
his action to remove John as Clinical Center Director.   I will come up with some options.  
See e-mail below:
RE  More thinking 
about JG.msg

Media coverage still intense.   Did Fox Cavuto Show today.   Also,
many quotes in numerous blogs and print news.
Will have dinner tomorrow night with John Gallin to try and help.

Dinner with John and Elaine Gallin.   John feels that he is being set up
for failure.   Francis wants him to stay on after he has essentially fired him by announcing 
that he is bringing in a CEO.   I am trying to fashion a position in the Clinical Center 
where John could function as the “Scientific Director” of the CC research programs of 
the various CC departments.   John will consider this.

Did MSNBC show on Zika.   Also, attended the IOM (NAM) meeting at
the NAS on Vaccines for emerging infections.   Gave opening talk on the need for 
establishing flexible vaccine platforms.   Meeting chaired by Adel Mahmoud and Marie-
Paule Kieny with Victor Tzau as the host.

Went to NYC today to receive the “Chivalry Award” from the American
Foundation of Savoy Orders, a 1000 year old Italian Organization of knighthood.   
Received it at a beautiful townhouse at .   Chris was with me.   Out to 
dinner after with Chris and Phil Piccigallo.

Gave CEO Luncheon lecture at the Army-Navy Club at Farragut Park on
17th Street, NW.
Also, this evening participated in a telebriefing for the constituents of Congresswoman 
Deborah Wasserman-Shultz (D-FL), which she moderated.  Did it with Steve Redd 
(CDC).   There were over 2000 call-ins on the phone.  Went very well.
May 20, 2016 – Big day!  Briefed President Obama in the Oval Office from 11:00 AM to 
12:20 PM.   Tom Frieden, Secretary Burwell, and I did a combined briefing.   I spoke 
predominantly about Zika vaccines and Tom handled the public health issues.   Present at 
the briefing were VP Joe Biden, Celia Munoz, Valerie Jarrett, Amy Pope, Susan Rice, 
Shaun Donovan (OMB), and Amy Rosenbaum (WH legisl).  Also, sat in (without 
comment) on the Press conference that the POTUS held in the Oval Office right after the 
briefing.   Went very well.  POTUS very familiar with me, Tom and what we are doing.

(Sunday) – Appeared on ABC This Week with George Stephanopoulos
to discuss Zika and my recent visit to the oval office with Obama.

Delivered Commencement Address at Yale University School of
Medicine.   Went extremely well.  Nice discussions with Jerry Friedland and Alison 
Galvani.

Went with Francis Collins to the Capitol to do a meet and greet with a
number of Republican and Democratic Congressmen set up by Pete Sessions (R-TX).   
They mostly asked about Zika and I held forth.   Tim Murphy, Mike Burgess, Fred 
Upton, Rosa DeLauro, etc.   Interesting that Congressman (Dr.) Burgess was insisting 
that I recommend to Obama to restrict travel for anyone to Zika areas, not just pregnant 
women.  He was not alone in this feeling.  I was surprised since Mike is an old friend and 
a good guy.
Went to Wilson Center and participated in a Zika Panel chaired by Jane Harman and 
Moderated my Jason Beaubien of NPR.   On panel - me, Anne Schuchat, and former 
Congresswoman Susan Molinari.  Jane and Susan were very, very complimentary of me 
for my “decades of amazing work on public health”.
Went with Bob Seder to Mets game.  Many home runs – Zimmerman, Rendon, Revere, 
Murphy, Ramos.   Francis Collins sang National Anthem!!

Press continues – appeared on CNBC “Squawk Box”.  Also, did KTSA
radio from Texas.  NPR from Houston and NPR from Miami.

Attended Annual Sons of Italy Gala at the Building Museum.   I received
the Lifetime Achievement Award here last year.   This year Condoleezza Rice received 
the award.   She sat at our table with Phil Piccigallo and the Italian Ambassador to the 
USA – Claudio Bisogniero.   We reminisced about out shared interactions (PEPFAR, 
etc.) during the Bush 43 White House years.   Joe Montegna was Master of ceremonies 
and Gary Sinese was special guest.

Press continues with Zika.  Also, report of mcr-1 gene (resistant to
Colistin) in an E.coli in a woman in Pennsylvania.  Press continues → CNN; Wall Street 
Journal; Bloomberg TV; “Environmental Health perspective” published by NIEHS; 
Steele and Ungar Radio Show.

(Memorial Day weekend)  Did CNN NewDay on Zika and MCR-1 gene
bacterial resistance.

Much media today on Zika as well as MCR-1 gene found in an E.coli in
a woman in Pennsylvania.   This gene leads to resistance to colistin (last line drug) - 
WTOP radio on Zika and MCR-1; also did CNN NewDay again.   Also, did Reuters TV; 
Katy Kay at BBC TV; NY Times interview; MSNBC with Chris Hayes

Honduran pregnant women infected with Zika in Honduras comes to
USA on vacation and delivers a microcephalic baby in Hackensack, NJ
I do MSNBC with Andrea Mitchell; NBC Nightly News.
MISSING MATERIAL (Ransomware hack) – June 2 through July 13, 2016 – will 
try to backfill

Went to NYC to the UNSpecial Session on HIV/AIDS and presented in a
panel with Michel Sidibe and Deb Birx on how we can end the AIDS pandemic.   I gave 
my usual talk on the scientific basis for the feasibility of doing this.   “We have the 
tools….”.

Briefed the democratic Steering and Outreach Committee in the
Mansfield Room of the US capitol together with Sylvia and Tom Frieden on an update of 
Zika and why we desparately need the money.
Received President’s Award from the President of Georgia (given by the Ambassador) on 
the celebration of the 25th Anniversary of the independence of the country of Georgia.   It 
was held on the rooftop terrace across from the capitol.

Continue to do press virtually every day on Zika.  Did CNN TV this
evening.

Did Zika briefing at the White House for Community people in EEOB
350.

Did a meet and greet with mostly GOP House members in Room H-314
(Rules Committee) of the Capitol.  Meeting called by Rep. Pete Sessions of Texas.  Good 
“back and forth”.   Francis Collins and I.  Most discussion about Zika.

Did Aspen Ideas Festival.  Was on Zika Panel with Anne Schuchat
and Rob Califf, chaired by Jeff Goldberg of The Atlantic.   Also did panel on drug 
development chaired by Helen Branswell of STAT. really enjoyed the trip!

Had beautiful reception at the Canadian Embassy in my honor for
receiving the Gairdner Global Health Award.   Many friends from NIH and elsewhere 
attended.   Also, Denise and Jack, Joanne and Jim, etc.

Meet with the POTUS in the Oval Office of the White House together
with Tom frieden and Sylvia Burwell to update him on the Zika situation.   The Congress 
has still not appropriated the money for Zika that the POTUS has requested ($1.9 billion) 
and there is a pissing match back and forth between the Dems and the GOP regarding the 
funding.   The GOP want to give the money but with “poison pill” provisions such as 
taking the money from the Affordable Care Act and from the Ebola account and they 
want to unfund Planned Parenthood.   The Dems reject this and the Congress will leave 
for their 4th of July break without acting

Much press exposure for me virtually every day associated with Zika
and my explaining the need for money for vaccine, etc.  Congress leaves for the 
Convention and for the summer break without an Zika Appropriations.   The press are 
pounding them (mostly the GOP) for playing politics with a public health crisis.

60 Minutes did filming here at VRC on Zika and took footage to do a
profile on me in the future.

Trip to Durban, South Africa for the 21st International AIDS Society
(IAS) meeting.   Gave Keynote at the CURE Symposium; received the President’s Award 
from the IAS.   Great meeting.   Much praise and recognition.
Now have 2nd person in Florida with local transmission of Zika!! – a male with no 
possibility of sexual transmissions to him; first person a few days ago was a 23 yo 
pregnant woman.   Had important phone call at 9:00 PM with HHS Secretary Burwell, 
Tom Frieden, me and others from HHS on how we will handle the contentious issue of 
potentially doing a travel alert for Florida for pregnant women, which would trigger the 
questions of what do you do with pregnant women who live in the Florida region.   State 
authorities, particularly Texas are very upset about the possibility of CDC issuing a travel 
alert for their state.   As usual, Sylvia Burwell either e-mails or calls me after the 
conference calls and seeks my independent counsel regarding sensitive policy issues.

I was attacked by “Ransonware” and my entire unprotected folder (C
Drive – Word Files) was encrypted.   Luckily, I had a backup of most of my historical 
daily notes and my autobiography was on a separate, nonaccessible folder.    However, I 
lost all of the letters that I have ever written as well as other important documents in the 
Word Files folder.   I had originally created this folde for the confidential files that I 
made right after the anthrax attacks since I did not want them accessible to anyone.   
However, I soon began putting other important documents into that folder – Bad idea!!!

Continuing to do much “local” media (local TV and Radio stations as
well as local NPR stations) set up by HHS to update on Zika and continue to pressure the 
Congress (which has not recessed for the summer) to appropriate the money for Zika.   
Democratic Convention this week.   Michelle Obama gave an amazing speech endorsing 
Clinton.   She spoke about her children and their future in America.   Bill Clinton also 
gave a great speech “humanizing” Hillary.

Great speeches at Dem Convention by VP Joe Biden and Obama.   Still
doing Zika press. Much local press given the local transmitted cases in Florida:  NPR 
Radio in California – KNX radio; ABC – KSAT Kansas (TV); WMBF – TV – Myrtle 
beach; WAMC radio Albany.

As predicted, it is happening!   Two more local transmitted cases (total =
4, at least) in Florida.   FDA ordering no blood collections for transfusion in Dade and 
Broward Counties until they can implement blood screening.   I taped for tonight PBS 
NewsHour and NBC Nightly News.  Continue local media: KJZZ Radio – NPR; WRC 
NBC local with Doreen Gentzler

Now confirmed total of at least 4 local transmission.   Governor Scott
from Florida confirms.   Much discussion here at HHS regarding if/when to issue a travel 
alert to pregnant women not to travel to Miami-Dade and Broward Counties where local 
infections are.   Continue to do local media:  WSVN TV Miami; KNBC TV – Los 
Angeles; WINA Radio – Charlottesville; Radio KSTX – San Antonio; Also did CNN 
with Wolf Blitzer. Also, did BBC TV via phone where they showed my picture on the 
screen.
Also, on reviewing data I realize that we should probably be doing an Alum Adjuvant 
arm to the HVTN 702 trial in addition to the MF59 adjuvant arm.   Looking at data from 
Feffa Franchini (NCI), she found that in a NHP model to reproduce RV144 in the 
monkey, she found that MF59 arm did not protect, whereas the Alum arm did.   Also, 
both arms gave the important antibody against V2 (the key cyclc dipeptide), while MF59 
also gave response to V1.   Could be that although MF59 is a more potent adjuvant than 
Alum, it induces an antibody response (against V1) that hinders the protective effect of 
the alum limb.   I will convene the HVTN 702 group to discuss adding an Alum arm to 
the trial in Africa.

Spoke over the phone with Carl Dieffenbach, Larry Corey, and Bart
Haynes about the issue with Feffa’s study and HVTN 702.   Spoke (as usual) with Tom 
Frieden by phone.   He is frustrated by the fact that that HHS and Secretary Burwell seem 
to distrust the CDC and Tom and continually micromanage them.   He is partially correct 
since HHS (Sylvia) often calls me to validate what Tom tells them.

(Sunday)– Appeared on Sunday AM “Face the Nation” talking about the
locally transmitted cases of Zika. Show went extremely well.   One of the best that I have 
done.   John Dickerson has now evolved into one of the best Sunday Show hosts.  I 
predicted that there would be more cases soon and that we would not hesitate to declare a 
travel alert for pregnant women to the area in the restricted region inside Dade County.   I 
found out from Tom Frieden after the show that there wer now additional symptomatic 
and asymptomatic cases (total 14) within that restricted area.   Together with the Florida 
Health Authorities, we will issue a travel alert for pregnant women for this restricted area.   
Testing is going on around the “rim” of this area.   I suggested to Tom that we add a 
cushion rim of restriction now.   He wants to wait until we test the rim (tomorrow) before 
we do this.   The Florida health authorities will go nuts if we issue an alert for the entire 
Dade County that includes Miami. It would destroy tourism even if it is only an alert for 
pregnant women.   England has already issued a travel alert for pregnant British women 
for the restricted area.   I am not concerned about the tourism.   If there are cases around 
the rim tomorrow I will push for widening the restriction.
Big conference call at 3:00 PM with Secretary Burwell to discuss situation.   We are 
having a terrible heat wave (>20 days in July >90 degrees F).
NY Times Sunday article on Obama being a science nerd.   Had me quoted about his visit 
to nancy Sullivan’s lab in the VRC and how he addressed the scientific community in 
Masur auditorium and blew the audience away with science talk.   Article by Gardiner

This amazing article by Laurie Garrett appeared in Foreign Policy on August 1, 2016
Dear Washington: The Time to Prepare 
for Zika Has Come and Gone
Act now, or bear the blame for the virus's devastating effects.
• By Laurie Garrett
• August 1, 2016
Dear presidential candidates, senators, and congressional representatives:
Get your butts back to Washington immediately.
The time you’ve had to get a preparedness plan in order but have wasted twiddling 
thumbs and shifting around budgets to make it look like you were taking the threat of 
Zika seriously is over. So, go behind closed doors to negotiate if the glare of the media 
and prying eyes of your constituencies is uncomfortable — I don’t care. But know this: 
The goal is to prevent a major pandemic from sweeping the nation, the births of 
thousands of Zika-deformed and neurologically impaired babies, to forestall adult cases 
of Guillain-Barré syndrome, eye problems, and other rare disorders caused by Zika 
infection, as well as to prevent the devastation of other public health and safety programs 
in cities, counties, and states across America as they shift resources from one account to 
another.
If I were the referee for your negotiations — which ought to commence this week in light 
of Florida’s local mosquito-carried Zika cases — the allowable focus for partisan debate 
between the houses of Congress and the White House would be extremely narrow. I 
would rule everything from the future of Planned Parenthood to pesticide regulations, 
shifting money from Ebola responses and existing federal and state accounts, the budget 
deficit, national debt — all off the table. The one, and only, topic open for debate? How 
much new money must be allocated on an emergency basis to meet the needs of the 
nation’s scientists, public health leaders, hospitals, maternal health providers, and 
mosquito and environmental health experts in order to limit the number of Americans 
who fall ill to Zika, pass the virus sexually to their partners or in utero to their fetuses, 
miscarry, or are born with neurological deficits and deformations.
Your mandate starting now: Show me the money.
Partisan bickering about the lives of American babies is unconscionable. This is no time 
for grandstanding. As of Aug. 1, 161 days have elapsed since the White House requested 
$1.9 billion in emergency funds for Zika, met by various counterproposals from the 
House and Senate Republican leaderships. That’s 161 days during which researchers and 
public health experts have struggled, with no new resources of any kind, to figure out 
how the virus works, find ways to control it, work on vaccines and treatments, and 
develop effective mosquito-control tactics.
If, politicians, you truly care about the right of every baby to a healthy life, you have no 
excuses, no rationales, and, yes, you will pay a price in upcoming elections if you fail. I 
don’t personally care whether you are Democrat or Republican, and neither will the 
voters living in regions that get slammed by the virus. The only question pregnant 
women, worried that they might be carrying a severely deformed child, will be asking is 
this: What did you do in the first week of August, once Zika was in Floridian mosquitoes, 
to protect my family from the newly arrived birth-defect-causing virus?
And here’s the thing: Americans aren’t stupid and won’t be hornswoggled. According to 
recent polls, most people in the United States know what Zika is and were concerned 
about it well before the virus infected Floridian Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. We have, as a 
nation, watched the epidemic reach our shores in slow motion, starting in mid-2015 when 
the Brazilian government 
issued its first announcements about babies born with 
microcephaly — literally, squashed brains and misshapen skulls. Six months ago, on Feb. 
1, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared a global Zika emergency. Americans 
looked south throughout our winter as the infected mosquitoes popped up across most of 
South America, Central America, and the Caribbean and as cases of microcephaly and 
other tragic disorders mounted.
Shortly after Florida’s governor, Rick Scott, announced on Friday that four people in 
Miami had contracted Zika from local mosquitoes, the nation’s most venerated epidemic 
scientist held his own press conference in Washington. Anthony Fauci, who has directed 
the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases for more than 30 years, soberly 
said that “we are watching a pandemic in process” and that he was “almost certain that 
we will see more cases across the United States.” On Monday, Scott confirmed 10 more 
homegrown cases of Zika in Florida.
And the rob-Peter-to-pay-Paul approach Fauci’s agency has had to use for 161 days in 
order to conduct Zika research in the absence of emergency funding? “We are getting to 
the point very, very soon that we are going to run out of the money that we are borrowing 
from ourselves,” Fauci said in a Friday briefing at the Bipartisan Policy Center in 
Washington.
You should pay heed to Fauci — this man has a long and storied track record on 
epidemics. He has been running the NIAID longer than anybody has ever directed any of 
the nation’s major scientific institutions, starting in the early 1980s when a mysterious 
form of cancer and lung disease was cropping up among gay men — that turned out to be 
the dawn of the AIDS pandemic. And it was Fauci who warned Presidents Ronald 
Reagan, George H. W. Bush, and Bill Clinton that all three presidencies were failing to 
grasp the scope, severity, and urgency of AIDS. The first president to take Fauci 
seriously was George W. Bush, who created the multibillion-dollar President’s 
Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), which today is credited with dramatic 
reductions in HIV deaths all over the world.
But the Brooklyn-born scientist who has given his entire career to public service wasn’t 
just right about HIV; Fauci has correctly advised five presidents and hundreds of 
members of Congress about SARS in China, the 2009 bird flu and H1N1 influenza 
outbreaks, multidrug-resistant tuberculosis in New York, the dangers of the anthrax 
spores mailed to media and politicians in 2001, hantavirus in New Mexico, Ebola in West 
Africa and in Dallas — the list is so long it would fill pages.
So, American politicians, ignore me if you wish, shrug off the Centers for Disease 
Control and Prevention if you are so inclined, poo-poo the WHO, and turn your back on 
the Floridian governor if you can — but open your ears when Tony Fauci speaks.
On June 6, Fauci warned Francis Collins, the director of the National Institutes of Health, 
and his advisors that Zika poses a threat unlike any we have previously faced. Research 
funds were urgently needed, Fauci said, to understand how the once-benign and largely 
ignored mosquito virus transformed into the greatest threat to pregnant women and their 
babies since the 1964 rubella epidemic. In the pre-vaccine 1960s, rubella, or German 
measles, was the primary cause of child blindness, deafness, miscarriage, and other 
congenital abnormalities in the United States. But Zika is actually worse than rubella 
because the virus feeds on neural progenitor cells, turning the would-be baby brain cells 
into Zika virus production factories and eventually burning the cells out. One by one, a 
nerve cell destined to control hearing, or vision, or memory, or balance, is killed off. The 
thousands of microcephalic babies born so far in South America and the Caribbean have 
had so many of their brain cells devoured by voracious viruses that there literally was 
insufficient mass to, as happens in normal fetal development, push the cranial bone 
upward to form a nice round skull.
But we have only begun to appreciate the range of neurological disorders Zika is 
inflicting on a generation of babies, because most of the afflicted are still too young to 
have reached key developmental markers, such as the ability to hold their head upright, 
capacity to recognize their parents, and the full range of hearing, walking, talking, and 
learning. Taking a page from cytomegalovirus (CMV), which can also be passed in utero 
from mother to fetus, only a small percentage suffer microcephaly and obvious 
deformities, while far larger numbers experience a 
vast array of learning deficits and 
brain dysfunctions that only become apparent later in childhood. Many psychiatric 
disorders that may be overlooked in infancy or early childhood are now known to stem 
from maternal viral infections damaging fetal brain development, including CMV, Borna 
disease virus, influenza linked to schizophrenia, herpes simplex virus (type 1) linked to 
bipolar disorders, and a long list of other fetal infections causing everything from autism-
like syndromes to acute depression long after the infected child’s birth.
Enough is enough, politicians. Pay heed to Puerto Rico, which, though it is a territory not 
a state, is inhabited by U.S. citizens.
Enough is enough, politicians. Pay heed to Puerto Rico, which, though it is a territory not 
a state, is inhabited by U.S. citizens. For months, Fauci, the CDC, and Puerto Rican 
health authorities have warned that a potentially catastrophic Zika epidemic was coming 
and pleaded for resources to address the crisis. The numbers of infected, symptomatic, 
and, yes, microcephalic babies were negligible for many weeks. But now, the word 
“crisis” is literally applicable to the island’s situation, as Zika diagnoses are soaring and 
the CDC on Friday declared, “The situation in Puerto Rico warrants urgent, 
comprehensive action to protect pregnant women.”
A month ago, Puerto Rico’s mosquito problems and Zika spread seemed manageable — 
just as Florida’s now appear — but today, despite aggressive mosquito-control efforts 
and public education campaigns, the population is beset by viral threat, with the number 
of diagnosed cases (which represent less than 20 percent of actual infections, most of 
which are asymptomatic) increasing by 1 percent per week. Consider this: A 1 percent 
increase in the first week of June may seem trivial, but by the first week of August, it is a 
9 percent increase, by Labor Day a 14 percent jump, and soon tens of thousands of Puerto 
Ricans will have been symptomatically infected with Zika, suffering from symptoms and 
side effects including mild fevers and rashes, paralysis, miscarriage, and giving birth to 
deformed babies.
And this entire explosive spread in Puerto Rico will transpire before Congress returns to 
Capitol Hill from summer recess.
Come on, congressional representatives and senators: This is a pandemic in progress. 
Reconvene immediately, negotiate a deal, focus on financing, and get the job — your job 
— done. Failure to do so will mean that every Zika-related birth defect, miscarriage, and 
paralysis case will be your fault.

My first visit to Cuba.   Met with various leading members of the
medical community (see below)
Stayed at the Hotel Nacionale de Cuba – an extraordinary place.   
It is the hotel that the Hollywood stars and celebrities of the 1940s and 1950s used to 
stay. It is also the iconic hotel represented by the famous scene in "The Godfather, Part 2" 
where Michael Corleone played by Al Pacino whispered in his brother Fredo's ear played 
by John Cazale; "Fredo, you broke my heart", fully intending to ultimately kill his own 
brother because Fredo betrayed him. It was a New Year's Eve party in the ballroom that I 
actually saw. It was the night that Fulgencio Batista abruptly left the party to escape from 
Havana to the Dominican Republic because Fidel Castro was outside of the city.
One of the most fun things that I have done in a long time was to drive to and from the 
hotel and restaurants in old town of Havana in the restored 1950s old cars for which 
Havana is famous. I only saw Havana, but it was actually very beautiful particularly the 
extraordinary shoreline that looks out into the Caribbean and the Straits of Florida. It is 
interesting that most of the people at least outwardly seem in awe of what Castro had 
accomplished for Cuba, particularly the health care system and the dramatic increase in 
literacy. I found it interesting that the leading physicians in Cuba have all heard of me 
and I was somewhat of a hero to them. In particular, several of them mentioned to me 
that they had read my early papers on vasculitis, they had studied from  Harrison's 
textbook of medicine and they were very familiar with my work on HIV AIDS. It was an 
unusual time in Cuba since I left for Cuba on a Sunday, and Fidel Castro had suddenly 
passed away at age 90 on the Saturday before the Sunday that I left. I almost made a 
wrong decision to cancel the trip. However, the Foreign Ministry of Cuba as well as the 
US ambassador (Amb De Laurentis) to Cuba insisted that we should go on with the 
Flavivirus Meeting, which had been co-organized between NIAID and the Cuban 
Ministry of health, who had visited me already twice over the past year. They felt that 
given Fidel's intense interest in medicine and science that it would be a show of respect 
for him if we went ahead with the meeting despite the declared nine days of mourning 
which actually began when I arrived on Sunday, November 27. The only difference in the 
atmosphere was that music was not played in the hotel lobby, which is usually a medlay 
of Latin American music. In addition, there was no music played in any of the restaurants 
that I went to, even though the atmosphere seemed very normal with many crowds in the 
restaurants.  
My impression of the Cuban scientists particularly those at the biotechnology center 
where Dr. Perez showed me around was that they were very oriented towards the 
development of products such as diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccines. In addition, 
almost everything they did related to peptide research, particularly in the arena of 
therapeutics. I gave the keynote address at the meeting which took place in the Hotel 
Nacionale. After that, I spent the two days that I was there visiting everything from 
individual doctor's offices, to polyclinics, to secondary hospitals, to tertiary hospitals 
where the most modern medicine was being practiced. I was particularly impressed by 
visiting the polyclinics which are closely connected with the individual private physicians 
of patients. Accessibility to the polyclinics for routine medical care actually took place on 
a 24-hour basis. In other words, if you had a medical or dental problem at any time of the 
day or night you could go to a polyclinic with there was someone on call 24 hours a day. 
If your problem was more severe than a routine issue, and ambulance or other form of 
transportation would take you to the appropriate facility at a higher level. I was told that 
there were hundreds of polyclinics scattered around Cuba.
In this street, hotel, and restaurants, there was a very friendly tone towards Americans. 
There was an extraordinary amount of tourism seemingly from all over the world, with 
only a relatively small percentage coming from the United States. President Obama has 
indicated that he wants to open up interactions and collaborations with the Cubans. We 
will have to wait and see whether this actually comes to pass under a Trump 
administration.

Trump Cabinet prior to their being sworn in and how I explained that there would 
certainly be an emerging ID crisis during the Trump administration.  7000 people in the 
auditorium.   I got standing ovation.   Great trip!

Next week CNN will air 90 minute documentary called “Unseen
Enemy”, which is a story about emerging infectious outbreaks – Ebola, Zika, pandemic 
flu, smallpox eradication, etc.   There is publicity surrounding the buildup to this.   I 
appeared this AM (Sunday) on C-SPAN “Washington Journal” with Janet Tobias, the 
producer of the film.   This evening will be on a panel with Sanjay Gupta as Moderator, 
Janet Tobias, Nahid Bhadella (Boston U), Peter Sands Chair of International Commission 
on a Global Health Framework for the Future and Richard Hatchett (new CEO of CEPI).  
Panel at the National Academy of Medicine (IOM) on 23 and C Street, NW.
Nest week I will go the NYC for another panel regarding the film as well as an 
appearance on CNN (see below).

Briefed HHS Secretary Price on the plans to develop and test vaccine for
the re-emerging H7N9 bird flu.
Also, Cliff Lane and I received report of the NAM on “Integrating Clinical research into 
Epidemic Response:  The Ebola Experience”.   We (NIAID, ASPR, FDA) commissioned 
the report to tell how we can do better.   Great report!   They came out strongly defending 
our stance during the Ebola outbreak that Clinical research is ethical to perform during 
outbreaks and importantly that RCTs are the optimal way to perform this research in an 
outbreak setting.

CDC announced that 10% of babies born in the USA to women who had
contracted Zika in Southern hemisphere of the Americas had congential abnormalities in 
brain.   I appeared on WTOP Radio to discuss this.

entries.content:
Went to NYC to appear in person with Anderson Cooper, Sanjay Gupta,
Janet Tobias and Irwin Redlener on a CNN Panel that will be shown together with the 
showing of the Documentary “Unseen Enemy”.  First time it will air is Friday, April 7, 
2017.   Will repeat at various future times.

Appeared on the “Situation Room” with Wolf Blitzer talking about the
upcoming film “Unseen Enemy” as well as emerging IDs in general.

Was supposed to fly to Detroit to give lecture at University of Michigan
(Ann Arbor) for their 200th Anniversary.  Went to airport and all planes cancelled due to 
bad weather in various parts of country that messed up the flight schedules.   Weather OK 
here and in Detroit.  Came back to NIH and David Awwad helped to set up my giving the 
lecture by video.   It worked very well.
The Panel discussion with Anderson Cooper and Sanjay Gupta aired tonight at 11:45 PM  
immediately after the showing of “Unseen Enemy”.   Looked real good.

Incredibly busy week with multiple talks: CUGH X2, HPTN, VAP,
among others.   Had dinner on April 12 at the home of Indian Ambassador Sarna on  
.   Amazing home and grounds.  Major confrontation with Russia 
coming up due to our condemning them for helping the Syrian government use sarin gas 
on their own civilians.

Got a call from Tim Ziemer (formerly the head of the President’s
Malaria Initiative (PMI) under president George W. Bush with continuation under 
Obama.   Tim informs me that he has been asked by the Trump people and accepted the 
position of the Director of Global Health Security and Biodefense at NSC.  He wanted to 
stay connected with me since he knows that when we have an outbreak, I am the ‘go to 
guy”.

Teleconference with TabAnsari going over a4B7 data in monkeys
showing depletion of CD8+ T cells + NK cells + NKT resulted in rebound of viremia.   
Now need to figure out which of these cell types actually suppressed viremia.

Went to PAHO with Lee Hall to meet with the “Leadership Group
(including me)” of the Decade of Vaccines.   Also there as part of group – Margaret Chan 
(WHO), Anthony Lake (UNICEF), Chris Elias (BMGF), Seth Berkley (GAVI).   We 
discussed the gaps in our approach to eliminating vaccine preventable diseases.   It was 
clear that the research agenda part of the effort (i.e. NIAID) was doing the best.

Went to Children’s National Medical Center to deliver a lecture on
ZIKA: One Year Later.   The people at Children’s had experience with Zika 
microcephalic and congenital abnormalities babies born in USA from travel-related Zika.   
Extremely positive reaction to my lecture.   See email below from a researcher at 
Children’s:
From: Kousa, Youssef @childrensnational.org] 
Sent: Tuesday, April 25, 2017 10:07 PM
To: Fauci, Anthony (NIH/NIAID) [E]
Subject: Thank You!
Dear Dr. Fauci, 
I hope that you are very well. I just wanted to sincerely thank you for coming to Children's 
National and giving a remarkable Grand Rounds lecture that we will continue to talk about in the 
days, weeks and months to come. 
I also wanted to sincerely thank you for giving me an opportunity to share with you my work on 
genetic risk factors in Congenital Zika Syndrome. Speaking with you about my project is a 
highlight in my training as a physician-scientist. 
Thank you so much once again and I look forward to sharing my results with you in the months 
and years to come. I am including below my contact information at Children's and NIH below.  
Best Regards, 
Youssef
-- 
Youssef A. Kousa, D.O., Ph.D., M.S., (PL-2)
Pediatric Residency Program 
Child Neurology Track
Children's National Health System
111 Michigan Avenue, NW
Washington, D.C. 20010
Pager: 
E-Mail: @cnmc.org
-- 
Youssef A. Kousa, D.O., Ph.D., PGY-2
Guest Researcher, Muenke Lab
National Human Genome Research Institute
National Institutes of Health
35 Convent Drive, Building 35
Bethesda, MD 20892-3717
E-Mail: @nih.gov
That night (April 24) I went to CSIS to deliver dinner talk on Malaria in conjunction with 
the Alan J. Magill Malaria Symposium.   Very nice reception to my talk.

Briefed Secretary Price on Pandemic and universal influenza vaccines in
the Humphrey Building (610F) conference room.   Also briefing were Anne Schuchat, 
Rick Bright, and George Korsch and Mitch Wolfe.

Went to Fischer’s Lane and gave lecture to Annual Meeting of VTEU’s.
Spoke on the situation in DC with Trump Budget, etc.   Gave them taste of reality of what 
the future will bring.
Went downtown to GW to lecture to the Elizabeth Glazer Pediatric AIDS Foundation – 
Spoke on Ending the AIDS Pandemic and remaining scientific challenges.   Extremely 
well-received with standing ovation.   Invited by CEO Chip Lyons.   Ran into old friends 
such as Jen Cohen, formerly of MSF.   One Ugandan Country Lead said at the end of 
lecture that he learned more in the 40 minutes of my lecture than he has in 10 years of 
lectures on AIDS.

Went to the 2017 Annual Garden Brunch before the White House
Correspondent’s Ball at Connie Milstein’s home ) hosted by Tammy 
Haddad, Kevin Sheekey, Hilary Rosen, Constance Milstein, Mark & Sally Ein, Fred 
Humphries, Kelley McCormick and Franco Nuschese.   Usual fun cast of characters.   
Had nice conversation with Don Lemon of CNN.   He praised my work; I told him how 
much I admired his courage in pushing back on his show the crazy “alternate truth” 
statement of Trump supporters like Jeffrey Lord.   He was very moved by my 
appreciation of what he is doing.   Also ran into Ian Kahn who plays George Washington 
on TV.   Spoke with his last year and today.   He told me that my conversation with him 
last year inspired him to use his role to try and make a differenc in pushing for 
responsibility and bipartisanship.  Also, spoke with Leslie Dach (former chief-of-staff to 
Sylvia Burwell); Bob Bennett (DC Lawyer); Hilary Rosen; Neera Tanden; Greta 
vanSusteren; among others.   Mostly a Democratic group bemoaning the craziness of the 
Trump administration.
President Trump did not attend the Ball (I was not invited this year).
Went to Children’s Inn Gala tonight at the Ritz Carlton Tyson’s Corner.

Went to premier first “partial” screening of the Discovery Channel 3 part
production of “First in Human” documentary on the NIH Clinical Center held at the 
Auditorium of the Ronald Reagan Building at 1300 Pensylvania Ave, NW.   Followed by 
panel chaired by Jon LaPook from CBS (my old friend).   Chris and I and Jon went out 
for a beer at the Willard Hotel across the street afterwards.  Jon is concerned and going to 
cover what looks like an outbreak of Zika in Brownsville, TX.
Interesting budget battles for NIH.   The House and Senate (led by Tom Cole and Roy 
Blount, respectively)  proposed an omnibus bill for a $2 billion increase for NIH for 
2017.

Visit to NIH of King Gustav of Sweden.   I presented our work on
Antibiotic resistance.   The King and the Swedish health authorities are very interested in 
the problem of AMR.
That evening Chris and I had amazing dinner (invited by Catherine and Wayne Reynolds) 
at the Jefferson Hotel.   Present at the dinner:  Secretary of State Rex Tillerson, Senate 
Leader Mitch McConnell, Transportation Secretary Elaine Choi, Viet Nam war hero 
General Jack Keane, Rick and Jane Atkinson, Justice Anthony Kennedy and wife Mary, 
Steve and Alice Rosenberg, Brendon and Mrs. Sullivan among others.
Rex Tillerson was quite open and transparent about the problems with North Korea and 
China.   He feels that we need to engage Kim Jong Un and convince him that we are not a 
threat to him.   China does not want to engage in hostilities.   They realize that if they lose 
soldiers in the context of the 1 child rule, then that family heritage stops.  They do not 
want war despite their building up of a military.   Also, China President Xi Jinping told 
him that when China engaged against us during the Korean War, it set back the one 
China effort 100 years.   If they engaged us now, it would destroy their economic growth.   
They do not want war.   And so he feels that if we do not try to embarrass them or 
interfere in their internal issues, that they will control Korea’s antics.
Also, I gave to the group under Catherine’s request an update on Zika, particularly Zika 
vaccine.   Mitch McConnell was quite complimentary to me about this.
Also, learned that my dear friend Bob Curran died .   I will 
go up to providence (Rumford), RI for his funeral on Monday, May 8.

Went to Rumford, RI for the funeral mass, burial (he was cremated and
his ashes buried in the cemetery, and then to the reception at the Brwn University faculty 
Club.   I am so glad that I went up for the event.  Bob’s wife Peg and his children Robert 
E. Curren III, Trevor and Victoria were thrilled to see me.  I was surprised to hear from 
people such as his ophthalmology nurses from his office that he “spoke about you all the 
time saying how you were his mentor and his very best friend forever”.   People I met 
who were his neighbors for the past 40+ years since he came back to Massachusetts/RI 
kept saying how Bob always used to talk about me and the great times we had together 
including our famous summer together touring Europe in our Deux Chaveau (French 
mini-car).  I had major flashbacks there and on the trip home about the truly amazing 
times that Bob and I had together.   We first met when I played against him in basketball 
in the St. Agnes of Rockville Center Tournament when we were 16 and 17 years old.   
We then were inseperable through college, medical school, internship/residency and then 
NIH.   He got married at end of residency and so after that he was more of a family man 
during the years at NIH.   Truly a great man and a dear, dear friend.

Briefed Sec. Price in Conference Room 610F of the Humphrey Building
on Antibiotic Resistance.   Together with CDC, FDA, BARDA, CMS, HRSA, etc.   
preparing the Secertary for his trip to the World Health Assembly in Geneva.   He is a 
very reserved man with a sense of humor.
Tonight, I drove in a rainshower from NIH to Baltimore for Bob Gallo’s 80th Birthday 
Party at the Grand Hotel on North Charles Street.   I gave one of the laudatios.   At my 
Table with Bob and MaryJane and also giving laudatios for Bob were:   former 
Governors Parris Glendening and Martin O’Malley; Kathleen Kennedy Townsend.  Hard 
to believe that Bob is 80 years old.  Had conversation with O’Malley about his 
Presidential run.   He is as shocked as everyone about Trump.   He said he never had a 
chance against Hillary since she had her machince, which actually messed up completely 
in the general election.

(Monday) – Did a 2 hour tape for a CBS special on HIV/AIDS – an
historical look to air on CBS Sunday Show.   The shoot was run by Rita Braver (Bob 
Barnett’s wife).  
Bright, sunny crisp, clear day, around 70 degrees F.  Went to West Wing of White House 
(6:00 PM) to meet with Reed Cordish (Assistant to the President) in preparation for a 
planned meeting the following day with President Trump on a multitude of issues: the 
usual vaccine/autism story; restriction in # of grants per investigator; Bayh-Dole Act; 
economic impact of NIH research.   The meeting was mostly for Francis, but Francis 
wanted me along for my “gravitas” and my experience with vaccines.   Also, Larry Tabak 
was there.   Reed had agreed to have all of us meet with the President tomorrow, but the 
agenda was packed for a 30 minute planned meeting in the Oval Office.   I cancelled 2 
lectures for tomorrow to be at the WH.   At the pre-brief meeting today were:  Chris 
Liddell (Assistant to the POTUS, whom I met at the dinner at the British Ambassador’s 
house several weeks ago – really good guy- New Zealander); Mary-Sumpter Lapinsky 
(HHS); Katy Talento (Domestic Policy Coouncil).   Towards the end of meeting, Reed 
mentioned that the agenda for tomorrow’s meeting would have to ultimately be approved 
by Ivanka Trump who had just left for a dinner.   Also, the # of people at the meeting 
tomorrow would have to be approved by her.   As it turned out, after we left the WH and 
I go home, Larry and Francis e-mailed me and forwarded an e-mail from Reed saying 
that Ivanka changed the agenda to 1 tiem – the NIH budget for 2018 and she wanted a 
small meeting with just Francis and Secretary Price.   Thus, Larry and I are “scratched”.   
Too bad I cancelled the lectures.   However, I got to meet Reed and Chris (again) and 
Katy.   Also, I know now who actually runs the White House agenda – Ivanka.

Testified at the House Appropriations Subcommitteee Hearing at 10:00
AM.   Chair:  Tom Cole (R-OK).   Despite the Trump budget asking for >20% cut in the 
NIH budget, it was a love fest for NIH with everyone (GOP and Dems) saying that they 
will actually increase the NIH budget as they had just done with the Omnibus Bill for FY 
2017 in which they increased the NIH budget by $2 Billion over FY2016.   I had the 
opportunity to “eloquently” (as said by many) defend the Fogarty International Cwenter 
(FIC) that the Trump Budget statement abolished.

Testified before the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on
oversight and Investigations on Zika.   Chaired by Tim Murphy (R-PA).   Hearing went 
very well.   Many questions aimed at me regarding progress on the Zika vaccine.   
Overall, very friendly.  I bailed out Lyle Peterson (CDC) a few times when he was in 
trouble.   He was very thankful.
Tonight I receive e-mail from:
 
Susanna Visser, DrPH, MS
Associate Director for Policy
Division of Vector-Borne Diseases
National Center for Emerging and Zoonotic Infectious Diseases
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
She thanked me for being so supportive of CDC.   Very nice e-mail.   Also, Tom Frieden e-
mail me saying that he was thinking of me and missed our relationship.   He hinted that 
he has accepted his “dream job” but could not give details at this point.   More later.

Presented my “State of NIAID” talk to the Annual HVTN meeting at the
Omni Shoreham Hotel in DC.   Spoke about the Trump budget (-26% for NIH) as well as 
the expanded Mexico City Policy and other items of interest.

Low level press continues on a variety of issues.   Today did Swedish
Public Radio on progress in Zika vaccines.

Very interesting and somewhat disturbing day.   Met with Robert F.
Kennedy, Jr. together with Francis Collins, Larry Tabak, Josh Gordon, Diana Bianchi, 
Linda Birnbaum and people from RFK, Jr’s inner circle.   RFK, Jr asked for the meeting 
(in medical Board Room – 4th Floor Clinical Center) to talk about the danger of vaccines 
including, but not limited to thimerasol and autism.   Sadly, he went on for over 1 hour 
stating points that were clearly inaccurate.   One example – he listed a whole bunch of 
diseases of various organ systems and said that these diseases were definitely caused by 
vaccines.   It was a very painful 2 hours spent with him.   He distorts the literature and 
denies anything that argues against him   Reed Cordish from the White House was at the 
meeting.   The meeting occurred since Jared Kushner wanted us to meet with RFK, Jr. in 
order to report back to President Trump who seems enamoured of RFK, Jr.   Cordish got 
the point about how off base RFK, Jr is.   RFK, Jr has serious spastic dysphonia and it 
was difficult to understand him, which was complicated by the emotional effort that he 
put into his presentation.   I actually felt very sorry for him since he clearly means well, 
but is completely incorrect in his information.   After it was over, I went back to him as 
he was leaving Building 10 and told him that although I explicitly said in the meeting that 
I totally disagree with most of what he said and I believe that he is fundamentally 
incorrect in his statements and conclusions, nonetheless, I admire and respect him for his 
passion in trying to protect children from harm.  He was very moved and told me that 
coming from me, this meant a lot to him.   We shall see where this goes vis-à-vis the 
POTUS.

Spent the better part of today with Bill Gates who made his yearly visit to
NIH.   I was on a panel with him in the Porter Building, I introduced another panel and 
importantly, I took 1hour and showed him around the VRC.   He has always been very 
interested in my viewpoints on areas of common interest with the BMGF.   He has 
recently announced the creation of Medical Research Institue (MRI) centered in Boston 
and Seattle ($100 million) to pursue research and importantly translational development 
in TB, Malaria, and enteric diseases.   He hopes to collaborate with me and NIAID in 
these endeavors.

Had major appearance in a CBS Special for Sunday AM on “CBS Sunday
Morning” .   Subject was 36 years of HIV/AIDS.  Rita Braver (Bob Barnett’s wife) was 
the producer.

Beautiful 70 degree dry Monday in DC.   Most of the Senate
Appropriations Subcommittee members and their staff visited NIH today for several 
hours.   I hosted a 35 minute tour (with a introductory talk by me on the history of the 
VRC with John Mascola.  Visiting us were:   Sens. (Chairman) Roy Blunt (R-MO), Patty 
Murray (D-WA), Richard Durbin (D-IL), Lamar Alexander (R-TN), James Lankford (R-
OK), John Kennedy (R-LA) Jean Shaheen (D-NH), Susan Collins (R-ME).   Great visit.
This evening went to George Washington  Medical School (Ross Hall – Room 117) to 
participate (gave a laudatio) in the ceremony conferring the Murdock Head Chair 
Professorship of Medicine and Health Policy on Bopper Deyton.

Gave my annoual “career inspiration” talk to the IDSA Fellows, this time
at the Pooks Hill Marriott.   Spoke about my briefing the soon-to-be Trump Cabinet on 
the danger of emerging microbes and worked into this the importance of the discipline of 
ID.

Went to Holy Cross for my 55th year Reunion!!!   Yikes!   I was the
featured speaker for the Class, which was an interview of me on stage by my old friend 
Pete Deckers.   Also, took many questions from the audience of my classmates and their 
wives.   They much appreciated my presence.   I missed the fact that Bob Curran was not 
there having died just a few weeks ago.

Visited my cousin Reynard Milici in Haydensville, MA and spent a lot
of time with him showing Chris and me his studio with so many of his magnificent 
paintings.   He is truly a great artist.
That evening went to the home of Jamie Gorelick and Rich Waldron for their Annual 
Spring Garden Party.   Much conversation about the “craziness” of Trump, particularly 
around the testimony of James Comey before the Senate Intelligence Committee this past 
week.   Had conversations with Jamie (who is the laywer of Jared Kushner re: his 
“conflict of interest”, David Ignatius (Post), Fred Hiatt (Post), Ruth Marcus (Post), E.J. 
Dionne (Post).   All agreed that if Trump went under oath the way he is threatening to do 
to contradict Comey, he would likely lie under oath.

Gave tour of VRC to various members of media,    Mostly modern blogs
like “STAT”, etc.

Went to Boston to participate in the The Atlantic PULSE: “On the Front
Lines of Health Care”.  Done in collaboration with STAT.   Moderator of my panel which 
I did with Vanessa Kerry was Jeffrey Goldberg (Editor of the Atlantic).  We discussed 
panemic preparedness.   After the panel, I did a “Facebook Live” interview with Jeff.

Did an amfAR event in the Hart Senate Building.   Gave keynote on
“Ending the AIDS Pandemic – Follow the Science”.   Usual crowd there.  Also speaking 
were Deb Birx, Michel Sidibe, Ron Klain, Judy Woodruff chaired a panel.   Sens. Ed 
Markey and John Donnelly were there.

Was visited here at NIH by a group of 6 FBI agents who are scientists in
their science division.   I gave them a briefing on NIAID in 7A-18.   I will soon go down 
to FBI headquarters to lecture to the entire group.

Went to NYC to give the Keynote lecture at the Inaugural Meeting of
the Einstein-Rockefeller-CUNY CFAR headed by my former fellow Harris Goldstein.   
Great to see him again.   He was thrilled that his old mentor came up to NYC to do the 
Keynote.   Others include Michel Nussenzweig, Charles Rice.
Terrible thunder storms along the east coast NYC-DC corridor resulting in cancellation of 
all planes on way back from NYC.   Took Acela and coincidentally sat next to my old 
friend Cheryl Mills.   We discussed the situation with the Trump administration and also 
the unsuccessful run of Hillary Clinton and the book that I am reading on the campaign 
called “Shattered” by Jonathan Allen and Amie Parnes.   It was great to see Cheryl again.   
Her husband spends ½ of every week working with educating prisoners in the correction 
system in New Orleans and we will connect him with Megan.  We discussed the 
entrepreneurial work that Cheryl is doing in Ghana and Tanzania.   I asked her to give 
Hillary my love, whom she sees often.
Later that night went to dinner run by AAAS to discuss the state of biomedical research 
in the current environment.   The meeting was run by the people from AAAS (Rebecca?) 
and Harold Varmus, Shirley Tilghman, Bruce Alberts and Marc Kirschner.   I discussed 
my perspective on how to better fund early stage investigators (ESI) given the current 
controversy about the aging population of researchers.

Did Peruvian TV on Zika; Peru is apparently in a minor/moderate
outbreak despite the fact that there are now very few cases in Brazil and other South 
American countries.
Also, the situation is Washington gets crazier and crazier with former FBI Director 
Mueller leading an investigation into Russia’s tampering (by hacking) with our election 
to favor Trump.   Trump and his senior leaders (Kellyanne Connelly et al) continue to lie, 
evade, and talk gibberish).

Testified before the Senate Appropriatioons Subcommittee together with
Francis Collins, Gary Gibbons, Nora Volkow, Richard Hodes, Josh Gordon, and Doug 
Lowy.   I vigorously defended the FIC that the President/OMB want to eliminate.   The 
global health community have sent many e-mails to me praising me for defending FIC.   
During the Hearing the Senators, particularly the GOP senators (Blount, Lamar 
Alexander, et al) together with the DEMs (Patty Murray, Dick Durbin, Pat Leahy) made 
it clear that they would not accept the President proposal to cut NIH by 21%.   The have 
been saying that the PB is “dead on arrival”.
Much debate going on regarding the GOP trying to repeal and replace “Obamacare” 
(ACA).   The GOP proposal (AHCA – American Health Care Act) is getting resistance 
even from some GOP members.

Went to Aspen, CO to participate in the Aspen Ideas Festival –
“Spotlight Health”.  Great trip.  Great weather. Was on panels: a) “Preventing 
pandemics”; and  b) “A world without AIDS”.  Both panels went extremely well.  
Interacted with many colleagues – Judy Woodruff (The NewsHour), Jeff Goldberg (The 
Atlantic), former SG Vivek Murthy, Walter Isaacson, etc.).   Many young global health 
people wanted “selfies” with me.   It is still tough for me to see myself as the “icon” and 
“legend” that the young people see me as.   Had lunch with Carl (Fritz) Schiller and John 
Stauffer, both former classmates at Cornell and Carl did residency with me at NY 
Hospital.   Unfortunately, .   Gave me  
increased awareness of my mortality….and my age.   I really like Carl and how he has 
turned out.   I always admired him when he was a student with me at Cornell as he was 
always pushing the envelop – avid anti-war (Vietnam) activist; big fan of Che Gueverra.  
He is very much put togrether now.

Went to Berkley/Oakland to participate as as Commissioner in
the Lancet Commission on Tuberculosis chaired by Eric Goosby and Dean Jamison.   
Purpose is to fine tune plans to end global TB.   Good group including South African 
MOH Aaron Motsaoledi, Peter Small, and a variety of young disease modelers. I 
presented the NIAID research agenda.   Enjoyable and informative discussions.  
Absolutely beautiful weather.   Stayed at the elegant Claremont Hotel and Spa.   Had 
great dinner with Ali on evening of July 12 at nice place in Oakland called Barlago and 
then went directly to SFO for the red eye back to DC. Ali just was promoted at Twitter.  
She is amazing!!

Joe Grogan the PAD at OMB for Health visited NIH Clinical Center.   I
helped brief him together with Francis Collins.   I then showed him around the Special 
Clinical Studies Unit and explained how we responded to the Ebola outbreak and how we 
took care of the Ebola patients.   Stewart Simonson had arranged for Joe to come here.   
Also with him were Mary-Sumpter Lapinski (HHS) and an assistant to VP Pence.   Visit 
went very well.
That evening Chris and I took out to dinner Salim (“Slim”)  and Quarraisha Karim who 
were visiting NYC and DC from South Africa on way to the IAS meeting in Paris (where 
I will soon leave for).   Dined at Bistro Bis at the George Hotel on E Street, NW

See  below.   A recent publication of my media appearances during the
Ebola outbreak.
The Rachel Maddow Show / The MaddowBlog 
The Great 2014 Sunday Show Race
12/29/14 12:30 PM—Updated 12/29/14 02:14 PM 
By Steve Benen
A year ago, House Intelligence Committee Chairman Mike Rogers (R-Mich.) made more 
Sunday show appearances than anyone else in the country. This year, Rogers’ dominance 
was even more pronounced, though that’s only part of the larger story.
Just like last year, I tallied up the guests for “Meet the Press,” “Face the Nation,” “This 
Week,” “State of the Union,” and “Fox News Sunday,” and once again, Republican 
voices easily outnumbered their Democratic counterparts. In fact, this year was even 
more one-sided in the GOP’s favor.
 
The above chart shows every political figure who made 10 or more Sunday show 
appearances this year – based on Nexis transcripts and the shows’ archives – with red 
columns representing Republicans, blue columns representing Democrats, and purple 
columns representing those who aren’t part of either party. Rogers easily outpaced the 
field last year with 27 appearances, and this year, he did even better, making 30 
appearances. To put that in perspective, that works out to an average of roughly one 
appearance every 1.7 weeks (or 2.5 Sunday show appearances a month, every month for 
a year).
 
House Homeland Security Committee Chairman Mike McCaul (R-Texas) was the only 
other person to reach 20 appearances this year, though he still ended up trailing Rogers 
by a large margin. Sen. John McCain (R-Ariz.), a Sunday-show staple for a generation, 
was third with 15, tied with Dr. Anthony Fauci, the non-partisan head of the National 
Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, who made a flurry of media appearances to 
discuss the Ebola threat in the fall.
 
But further down the rankings, some interesting numbers pop up.
 
For example, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was one of the more popular 
guests this year, to the point that he made more appearances than any Democratic official 
in Congress or in the Obama administration. In fact, 15 people made 10 or more 
appearances on Sunday shows this year, and only three Democrats made the cut – and 
they’re all at the bottom of the list.
 
Of the 15 most frequent guests, 14 are men. All 15 are white.
 
I should note that for the purposes of this study, I excluded hosts and journalists, looking 
exclusively at current officials, former officials, candidates for public office, domestic or 
foreign policymakers, or anyone fairly characterized as actively involved in the political 
arena. (Karl Rove’s inclusion here is admittedly debatable, but given his role in the 
Crossroads operation, it seemed only fair to characterize him as someone who’s “in the 
arena.” He has a media role, to be sure, but Rove also hopes to directly influence the 
outcome of the elections on which he comments.)
 
There is a school of thought, articulated by the estimable Jonathan Bernstein among 
others, that says tallies like these are unimportant – whether Sunday shows prefer 
Republicans to Democrats is inconsequential, the argument goes, and hardly worth 
considering in any detail.
 
Obviously, I disagree. For me, the five major Sunday shows represent a political 
institution of sorts, highlighting the kinds of voices and ideas the Beltway media 
considers important. The discussions held on these programs help reflect – and in many 
cases, shape – the conventional wisdom for the political establishment in D.C.
 
And a little too often, these discussions suggest to the public that it’s Republicans whose 
views drive the conversations that matter.
 
Like last year, I’ll leave it to others to speculate as to why the Sunday shows seem so 
preoccupied with Republican guests, but I will note that msnbc offers fine programming 
on weekends, including Sunday mornings, featuring a diverse group of stories and guests 
unseen elsewhere.

Opinion | Roland Merullo
Christopher Columbus and Italian-
Americans: a sad marriage
David L. Ryan/Globe Staff/File
A statue of Christopher Columbus stood in the North End at a park named for the 
explorer.
By Roland Merullo   October 09, 2017 
When I was a boy, my father owned a book called “Columbus WAS First.” I never read 
it. I’m not sure he ever read it, either. But, judging by the title, I can guess what it argued, 
and I can guess why he kept it on the shelf.
Few, if any, modern historians dispute Christopher Columbus’s record of brutality or his 
pivotal role in the heinous practice of owning and selling human beings. Torture, punitive 
amputation, wholesale slaughter of the generally peaceful native peoples he encountered 
on his four voyages — none of that was rare among European explorers of his era. 
Columbus’s enthusiasm for it, though, while not putting him in a class by himself, 
certainly calls into question why we continue to celebrate a national holiday in his name. 
What’s painful to me, and I’m certain would have been painful to my father were he still 
alive, is that the holiday named for Columbus — chosen to mark the October day on 
which he first saw land he believed was the Far East — has become the one day each 
year on which the contributions of Italian-Americans are recognized. It’s a sad marriage. 
There’s so much to be proud of in the courage, resilience, and achievements of 
Americans who trace their heritage to the Italian peninsula — and so much to be ashamed 
of in the nation’s continued elevation of Columbus to hero’s status.
As this summer’s events in Charlottesville, Va., underscored, America has a lot to reckon 
with in terms of its history. Our land is littered with tributes to slave owners and other 
torturers, to the architects of genocide; some of our universities and libraries are named 
after people who made their fortunes by poisoning others, or from the sweat and blood of 
others. Their victims were people of color, yes, particularly and horribly, but also wave 
after wave of immigrants who happened to arrive a century or three later than the First 
Exploiters.
While it’s clear that our moral consciousness has evolved — behavior once endorsed by 
queens and bishops, presidents and popes, has become obviously evil in the eyes of the 
vast majority of Americans — we retain a tendency toward blind hero-worship. Athletes, 
politicians, CEOs, and celebrities of all stripes are admired for their successes while we 
often ignore their gross mistreatment of others, and of the earth.
Speaking as one Italian-American, I’ll have no problem when statues to Columbus are 
removed from the public eye. And I won’t mind at all if the second Monday in October is 
no longer a holiday that bears his name. It will bother me, though, if the grit, talent, and 
generosity of millions of Italian-Americans is no longer recognized. I could mention 
Enrico Fermi and Dr. Anthony Fauci, Mercury astronaut Walter Schirra, DiMaggio, 
Sinatra, De Niro, Madonna, and Lady Gaga, but I’d rather honor the nameless ones who 
kept house and raised kids, who toiled in shoe and textile factories and carved stone and 
worked the mines in Appalachia. Italian-Americans endured mockery and exclusion, then 
watched their culture — so rich in the arts, sciences, and human warmth — reduced to 
mob stereotypes and Jersey Shore goons. We deserve a special day. 
Roland Merullo’s latest novel is “The Delight of Being Ordinary: A Road Trip with the 
Pope and Dalai Lama.”
